title.zh: 卷十一 志第一 律志序
title.raw: 卷十一 志第一 律志序 Volume 11 Treatises 1: Lu Treatises Preface

sentences.zh: 左史記言，右史記事，事則春秋是也，言則尚書是也。

translations.literal: The left historiographer recorded words; the right historiographer recorded events. Events are what the Spring and Autumn Annals are; words are what the Documents are.
translations.idiomatic: The left historiographer kept the record of speeches; the right historiographer kept the record of events. Events became the Spring and Autumn Annals; speeches became the Documents.

sentences.zh: 至於楚書、鄭志、晉乘、楚杌之篇，皆所以昭述前史，俾不泯於後。

translations.literal: As for the chapters of the Chu Annals, the Zheng Records, the Jin History, and the Chu Chronicles, all were means to illuminate and set forth earlier histories, so that they would not be extinguished in later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Works such as the Chu Annals, the Zheng Records, the Jin History, and the Chu Chronicles all served to set forth earlier histories in full light, lest they be lost to posterity.

sentences.zh: 司馬遷制一家之言，始區別名題，至乎禮儀刑政，有所不盡，乃於紀傳之外，創立八書，片文隻事，鴻纖備舉。

translations.literal: Sima Qian fashioned the discourse of a single school, and for the first time distinguished titles by name. As for ritual, penal law, and government, there were matters he did not exhaust; therefore, beyond the annals and biographies, he established the Eight Treatises, so that fragmentary texts and isolated affairs, great and small alike, were all included.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Qian shaped his independent historical vision, he was the first to sort material under distinct topical headings. Where ritual, penal law, and administration still eluded full treatment, he went beyond annals and biographies to create the Eight Treatises, gathering every scrap of evidence, large or small.

sentences.zh: 班氏因之，靡違前式，網羅一代，條流遂廣。

translations.literal: The Ban clan followed him, not departing from the earlier pattern, and netted an entire age; the branches of classification thus grew broad.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu took up his model without breaking from the earlier form, sweeping an entire dynasty into his net until the topical branches spread wide.

sentences.zh: 律曆禮樂，其名不變，以天官為天文，改封禪為郊祀，易貨殖、平準之稱，革河渠、溝洫之名；

translations.literal: For pitch pipes, calendars, ritual, and music, the names did not change; he took the Heavenly Offices treatise as Astronomy, changed Feng and Shan into Suburban Sacrifice, altered the titles Goods and Wealth and Equalization, and changed the names of the River Works and Ditches and Channels treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch pipes, calendars, ritual, and music kept their old titles; he renamed the Heavenly Offices section Astronomy, turned Feng and Shan into Suburban Sacrifice, retitled Goods and Wealth and Equalization, and renamed the River Works and Ditches and Channels sections.

sentences.zh: 綴孫卿之辭，以述刑法，采孟軻之書，用序食貨。

translations.literal: He appended the words of Master Xun to set forth Penal Law, and drew on the book of Master Meng to arrange Food and Wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He drew on Xunzi to compose the treatise on penal law and on Mencius to order the section on food and wealth.

sentences.zh: 劉向鴻範，始自春秋，劉歆七略，儒墨異部，朱贛博采風謠，尤為詳洽，固並因仍，以為三志。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's Great Plan began from the Spring and Autumn period; Liu Xin's Seven Summaries divided Confucians and Mohists into different sections; Zhu Gan broadly collected folk songs and was especially thorough—Gu indeed followed and continued these, taking them as the three treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's Great Plan reached back to the Spring and Autumn era; Liu Xin's Seven Summaries separated Confucian and Mohist writings into different categories; Zhu Gan's wide gathering of folk songs was especially comprehensive. Ban Gu followed these lines as well, treating them as three treatises.

sentences.zh: 而禮樂疏簡，所漏者多，典章事數，百不記一。

translations.literal: Yet ritual and music were sparse and brief; what was omitted was great in number, and of statutes and regulations, affairs and figures, not one in a hundred was recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ritual and music were treated thinly, with much left out, and of institutional records and numerical data scarcely one item in a hundred was preserved.

sentences.zh: 天文雖為該舉，而不言天形，致使三天之說，紛然莫辨。

translations.literal: Although astronomy was treated in comprehensive scope, it did not speak of the form of Heaven, with the result that the various theories of the Three Heavens became confused and could not be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomy was surveyed at length, yet the shape of Heaven itself went unaddressed, so the competing doctrines of the Three Heavens fell into dispute with no way to settle them.

sentences.zh: 是故蔡邕於朔方上書，謂宜載述者也。

translations.literal: Therefore Cai Yong, in a memorial submitted from Shuofang, said that these matters ought to be recorded and set forth.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Cai Yong, writing from Shuofang, urged that such matters be fully recorded in the history.

sentences.zh: 漢興，接秦阬儒之後，典墳殘缺，耆生碩老，常以亡逸為慮。

translations.literal: When Han arose, it followed upon the age when Qin had blocked the Ruists; the canonical repositories were damaged and incomplete, and the aged scholars constantly took the loss and disappearance of texts as their concern.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty rose, it came after Qin's suppression of classical learning. The canonical libraries lay in ruins, and veteran scholars lived in constant fear that the tradition would be lost.

sentences.zh: 劉歆七略，固之藝文，蓋為此也。

translations.literal: Liu Xin's Seven Summaries and the Bibliographic Treatise of Ban—this was essentially for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin's Seven Summaries and Ban Gu's Bibliographic Treatise were created above all for that reason.

sentences.zh: 河自龍門東注，橫被中國，每漂決所漸，寄重災深，堤築之功，勞役天下。

translations.literal: The Yellow River, from Longmen eastward, flowed across China; wherever its floods spread, the calamity was grave and the burden heavy, and the work of building dikes taxed the labor of the empire.
translations.idiomatic: East of Longmen the Yellow River poured across the heartland of China. Each burst and shift brought disaster in its wake, and the endless labor of dike-building wore out the realm.

sentences.zh: 且關、洛高塏，地少川源，是故鎬、酆、潦、潏，咸入禮典。

translations.literal: Moreover the passes and Luo region stood on high ground with few rivers and sources; therefore the Hao, Feng, Liao, and Ju all entered the ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: The Guanzhong and Luoyang regions moreover stood on high ground with few natural waterways, which is why the Hao, Feng, Liao, and Ju were all enshrined in ritual texts.

sentences.zh: 漳、滏、鄭、白之饒，溝渠沾溉之利，皆民命所祖，國以為天，溝洫立志，亦其宜也。

translations.literal: The abundance of the Zhang, Fu, Zheng, and Bai canals and the benefit of irrigation by ditches and channels were both what the people looked to as the source of life; the state took them as its Heaven. To set forth the intent of ditches and channels was also fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The wealth of the Zhang, Fu, Zheng, and Bai waterways and the bounty brought by irrigation ditches were matters on which the people's lives depended and the state founded its very survival. A treatise on ditches and channels was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 世殊事改，於今可得而略。

translations.literal: Generations differ and affairs change; what can be set forth today may be treated in summary.
translations.idiomatic: Times change and institutions shift; what can be set down today must be treated in outline.

sentences.zh: 竊以班氏律曆，前事已詳，自楊偉改創景初，而魏書闕志。

translations.literal: I consider that Ban's treatise on pitch pipes and the calendar has already treated earlier matters in detail; from Yang Wei's reform and creation of the Jingchu [calendar] onward, the History of Wei lacks a treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu's sections on pitch pipes and the calendar already cover earlier matters in detail. From Yang Wei's Jingchu reform onward, however, the Wei history left no corresponding treatise.

sentences.zh: 及元嘉重造新法，大明博議回改，自魏至宋，宜入今書。

translations.literal: When the Yuanjia era again fashioned a new method and the Daming period broadly debated and revised it, from Wei through Song these ought to enter the present book.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanjia reign created a new calendar and the Daming reign debated further revisions, the calendrical work from Wei through Song belongs in this history.

sentences.zh: 班固禮樂、郊祀，馬彪祭祀、禮儀，蔡邕朝會，董巴輿服，並各立志。

translations.literal: Ban Gu's Ritual and Music and Suburban Sacrifice, Ma Biao's Sacrificial Rites and Ceremonial Protocol, Cai Yong's Court Assemblies, and Dong Ba's Chariots and Garments—each established a separate treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu wrote treatises on ritual, music, and suburban sacrifice; Ma Biao on sacrificial rites and ceremonial protocol; Cai Yong on court assemblies; and Dong Ba on chariots and garments—each as its own section.

sentences.zh: 夫禮之所苞，其用非一，郊祭朝饗，匪云別事，旗章服物，非禮而何？

translations.literal: What ritual embraces has more than one use; suburban sacrifice, court audiences, and feasts are not separate matters, and banners, insignia, garments, and implements—if not ritual, then what are they?
translations.idiomatic: Ritual embraces many functions at once. Suburban sacrifice, court audiences, and ceremonial feasts are not separate subjects, and banners, regalia, and vestments belong to ritual by their very nature.

sentences.zh: 今總而裁之，同謂禮志。

translations.literal: Now I gather and trim them together, jointly calling them the Treatise on Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore gathered these topics together under a single Treatise on Ritual.

sentences.zh: 刑法、食貨，前說已該，隨流派別，附之紀傳。

translations.literal: Penal law and food and wealth were already covered in the earlier discussion; following their separate streams, they are attached to the annals and biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Penal law and food and wealth were already treated in the earlier account; following their separate lines of development, they are attached to the annals and biographies.

sentences.zh: 樂經殘缺，其來已遠，班氏所述，政抄舉樂記，馬彪後書，又不備續。

translations.literal: The Music Classic was damaged and incomplete; its loss reaches far back. What the Ban clan set forth largely copied and excerpted the Record of Music; Ma Biao's Later History did not continue it completely.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Classic had long lain damaged and incomplete. Ban Gu's account largely copied from the Record of Music, and Ma Biao's Later History failed to carry the subject forward.

sentences.zh: 至於八音眾器，並不見書，雖略見世本，所闕猶眾。

translations.literal: As for the eight classes of sound and the many instruments, none appear in the book; although they are briefly seen in the World Roots, what is missing is still great in number.
translations.idiomatic: The eight categories of tone and the full range of instruments scarcely appear in the histories at all. Even the World Roots offers only glimpses, and much remains unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 爰及雅鄭，謳謠之節，一皆屏落，曾無概見。

translations.literal: Down to elegant and popular airs and the rhythms of songs and ballads, all were cast aside, with not even a general account preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Elegant court music and popular songs alike were cast aside, until not even a general account survived.

sentences.zh: 郊廟樂章，每隨世改，雅聲舊典，咸有遺文。

translations.literal: The hymns of suburban altars and temples changed with each age, yet the old standards of refined music still preserve surviving texts.
translations.idiomatic: Temple and suburban hymns changed from reign to reign, yet the old refined repertory still left texts behind.

sentences.zh: 又案今鼓吹鐃歌，雖有章曲，樂人傳習，口相師祖，所務者聲，不先訓以義。

translations.literal: Moreover, examining the present drum-and-bugle songs of the Music Office, although they have set tunes, musicians transmit them by oral teaching from master to disciple; what they pursue is sound, not first instructing them in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Music Office drum-and-bugle songs, though they retain their melodies, are handed down mouth to ear. Musicians care for the sound alone and are not first taught what the words mean.

sentences.zh: 今樂府鐃歌，校漢、魏舊曲，曲名時同，文字永異，尋文求義，無一可了。

translations.literal: Now the Music Office drum songs, compared with the old tunes of Han and Wei, share titles from time to time but differ completely in wording; seeking meaning in the text, not one can be understood.
translations.idiomatic: When one compares present Music Office drum songs with Han and Wei originals, the titles sometimes match but the words never do. Search the texts for meaning and nothing can be made out.

sentences.zh: 不知今之鐃章，何代曲也。

translations.literal: One does not know of what age the present drum sections are.
translations.idiomatic: No one can even say which age produced the drum songs in use today.

sentences.zh: 今志自郊廟以下，凡諸樂章，非淫哇之辭，並皆詳載。

translations.literal: In this treatise, from suburban altars downward, all hymn texts that are not licentious or vulgar are recorded in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: In this treatise, every hymn from suburban rites downward that is not licentious or vulgar is recorded in full.

sentences.zh: 天文、五行，自馬彪以後，無復記錄。

translations.literal: Astronomy and the Five Phases, from Ma Biao onward, were no longer recorded.
translations.idiomatic: From Ma Biao onward, astronomy and the Five Phases received no further historical record.

sentences.zh: 何書自黃初之始，徐志肇義熙之元。

translations.literal: He Chen's [work] began from the start of Huangchu; Xu Yi's began from the founding of the Yixi era.
translations.idiomatic: He Chen's account began with the Huangchu era; Xu Yi's with the founding of the Yixi reign.

sentences.zh: 今以魏接漢，式遵何氏。

translations.literal: Now, taking Wei as continuing Han, I follow the pattern of the He clan.
translations.idiomatic: Treating Wei as the continuation of Han, I follow He's model.

sentences.zh: 然則自漢高帝五年之首冬，暨宋順帝昇明二年之孟夏，二辰六沴，甲子無差。

translations.literal: Thus from the first month of winter in the fifth year of Emperor Gaozu of Han down to the first month of summer in the second year of Shengming of Emperor Shun of Song, for the two chronologies and six portents, the sexagenary cycle shows no discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: From the first month of winter in Han Gaozu's fifth year to the first month of summer in Song Shundi's second Shengming year, the two chronologies and six portents align through the sexagenary cycle without discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 聖帝哲王，咸有瑞命之紀，蓋所以神明寶位，幽贊禎符，欲使逐鹿弭謀，窺覬不作，握河括地，綠文赤字之書，言之詳矣。

translations.literal: Sage emperors and wise kings all had records of auspicious mandates, for thereby they made luminous the precious throne, secretly assisted the tokens of fortune, wishing to make those who strove for the realm lay down their schemes and cease their covetous glances; the books that grasped the river, enclosed the earth, and bore green script on red background spoke of this in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Sage rulers all possessed records of auspicious mandates by which they illuminated the throne and confirmed heaven's favor, hoping to still the ambitions of rival claimants. Texts that 'grasped the river,' 'enclosed the earth,' and bore green characters on red ground spoke of such things at length.

sentences.zh: 爰逮道至天而甘露下，德洞地而醴泉出，金芝玄秬之祥，朱草白烏之瑞，斯固不可誣也。

translations.literal: When the Way reached Heaven, sweet dew descended; when virtue penetrated Earth, sweet springs issued forth; the auspicious signs of golden fungus and black millet and the omens of vermilion grass and the white crow—these indeed cannot be denied.
translations.idiomatic: When the Way touched Heaven, sweet dew fell; when virtue penetrated the earth, sweet springs welled up. Omens such as golden fungus, black millet, vermilion grass, and the white crow cannot simply be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 若夫衰世德爽，而嘉應不息，斯固天道茫昧，難以數推。

translations.literal: If in a declining age virtue waned yet favorable responses did not cease, this is inherently because the way of Heaven is obscure and hard to calculate by number.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when virtue faded in a declining age while auspicious signs still multiplied, that too shows how obscure Heaven's way is and how poorly it yields to reckoning.

sentences.zh: 亦由明主居上，而震蝕之災不弭；

translations.literal: It is also because when a bright lord sat above, the disasters of quakes and eclipses were not stilled;
translations.idiomatic: It may also happen that a worthy ruler reigns above while earthquakes and eclipses continue unabated;

sentences.zh: 百靈咸順，而懸象之應獨違。

translations.literal: when the hundred spirits all complied, the responses of suspended omens alone went contrary.
translations.idiomatic: or that all spirits appear obedient while celestial signs alone refuse to accord.

sentences.zh: 今立符瑞志，以補前史之闕。

translations.literal: Now I establish a Treatise on Tokens and Omens to supplement what the earlier histories omitted.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore establish a Treatise on Tokens and Omens to fill the gaps left by earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 地理參差，事難該辨，魏晉以來，遷徙百計，一郡分為四五，一縣割成兩三，或昨屬荊、豫，今隸司、兗，朝為零、桂之士，夕為廬、九之民，去來紛擾，無暫止息，版籍為之渾淆，職方所不能記。

translations.literal: Geography is uneven and affairs are hard to cover completely; from Wei and Jin onward there were hundreds of migrations and changes—a single commandery was divided into four or five, a single county was carved into two or three; what yesterday belonged to Jing or Yu today falls under Si or Yan; men who in the morning were subjects of Ling or Gui in the evening became people of Lu or Jiu. Coming and going were tangled and restless, without a moment's pause; the household registers were thrown into confusion, and even the Director of Borders could not record them.
translations.idiomatic: Geography is uneven, and no account can fully compass it. From Wei and Jin onward territories were carved and re-carved countless times: one commandery became four or five, one county split in two or three. Lands that yesterday belonged to Jing or Yu might today answer to Si or Yan; people who at dawn were subjects of Ling or Gui by dusk were counted among the households of Lu or Jiu. Movement never ceased, registers fell into chaos, and even the office charged with mapping the realm could not keep pace.

sentences.zh: 自戎狄內侮，有晉東遷，中土遺氓，播徙江外，幽、并、冀、雍、兗、豫、青、徐之境，幽淪寇逆。

translations.literal: From the time the Rong and Di raided within the borders and Jin moved east, the remaining people of the central lands were scattered beyond the rivers; the territories of You, Bing, Ji, Yong, Yan, Yu, Qing, and Xu sank into darkness under the invaders.
translations.idiomatic: After the northern peoples invaded and Jin fled east, the remnant population of the central plains was driven beyond the rivers. You, Bing, Ji, Yong, Yan, Yu, Qing, and Xu were lost to the invaders.

sentences.zh: 自扶莫而裹足奉首，免身於荊、越者，百郡千城，流寓比室。

translations.literal: From the time they bound their feet and bowed their heads in submission, those who escaped with their lives to Jing and Yue numbered a hundred commanderies and a thousand cities, with exiles in every household.
translations.idiomatic: Those who bound their feet, bowed their heads, and fled south to Jing and Yue filled a hundred commanderies and a thousand cities, until exiles outnumbered natives in house after house.

sentences.zh: 人佇鴻雁之歌，士蓄懷本之念，莫不各樹邦邑，思復舊井。

translations.literal: People awaited the song of the wild geese; scholars nourished the thought of returning to their native wells—none failed to set up their own states and towns, thinking to recover their old homesteads.
translations.idiomatic: The people sang songs of longing like the wild geese's cry; scholars cherished the hope of returning home. Everywhere they founded new settlements in memory of the old.

sentences.zh: 既而民單戶約，不可獨建，故魏邦而有韓邑，齊縣而有趙民。

translations.literal: Afterward households were few and families sparse, and they could not be established separately; therefore within Wei territory there were Han towns, and within Qi counties there were Zhao people.
translations.idiomatic: But households were few and could not stand alone, so Han communities appeared inside Wei territory and Zhao families inside Qi counties.

sentences.zh: 且省置交加，日回月徙，寄寓遷流，迄無定託，邦名邑號，難或詳書。

translations.literal: Moreover, as provinces and districts were repeatedly added and abolished, shifting day by day and month by month, those lodged elsewhere wandered without fixed settlement; the names of states and towns were hard to record in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and districts were added and abolished month by month; migrants wandered without fixed abode, and the names of states and towns could scarcely be written down in full.

sentences.zh: 大宋受命，重啟邊隙，淮北五州，翦為寇境，其或奔亡播遷，復立郡縣，斯則元嘉、泰始，同名異實。

translations.literal: When Great Song received the mandate, the frontier was reopened; the five provinces north of the Huai were cut off as enemy territory. Where fugitives fled and were scattered, counties and commanderies were re-established—thus under Yuanjia and Taishi, names were the same but the reality differed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song dynasty arose, the northern frontier was reopened, yet the five Huai-north provinces became enemy ground. Refugees who fled south re-established old commanderies and counties in name only—so under Yuanjia and Taishi, the same names concealed different realities.

sentences.zh: 今以班固、馬彪二志，晉、宋起居，凡諸記註，悉加推討，隨條辨析，使悉該詳。

translations.literal: Now, taking the two treatises of Ban Gu and Ma Biao, the Jin and Song court records, and all relevant commentaries, I add thorough investigation, analyzing each entry so that all may be covered in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on Ban Gu and Ma Biao, on Jin and Song court records, and on every relevant commentary, I have traced each entry so that the account may be as complete as possible.

sentences.zh: 百官置省，備有前說，尋源討流，於事為易。

translations.literal: The establishment and abolition of the hundred offices all have earlier explanations; tracing the source and pursuing the stream is easy in practice.
translations.idiomatic: The creation and abolition of the hundred offices already have earlier accounts; tracing origins and following their course is the easier part.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，東海何承天受詔纂宋書，其志十五篇，以續馬彪漢志，其證引該博者，即而因之，亦由班固、馬遷共為一家者也。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era, He Chengtian of Donghai received an edict to compile the History of Song. His fifteen treatises continued Ma Biao's Han Treatises; where his citations were comprehensive and well supported, I follow them directly—this too is because Ban Gu and Sima Qian together form a single tradition.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era He Chengtian of Donghai received orders to compile the History of Song. His fifteen treatises continued Ma Biao's Han Treatises; where his evidence is sound I follow it, for Ban Gu and Sima Qian belong to one continuous tradition.

sentences.zh: 其有漏闕，及何氏後事，備加搜采，隨就補綴焉。

translations.literal: Where there are omissions and gaps, and matters after He's time, I have searched and collected broadly, supplementing wherever needed.
translations.idiomatic: Where he left gaps, and for events after his day, I have searched widely and filled in what was missing.

sentences.zh: 淵流浩漫，非孤學所盡；

translations.literal: The source stream is vast and cannot be exhausted by solitary learning;
translations.idiomatic: The stream of learning is vast, far beyond what one scholar can master;

sentences.zh: 足蹇途遙，豈短策能運。

translations.literal: the foot is lame and the road long—how can a short whip drive the journey?
translations.idiomatic: with lame feet on a long road, no short whip can carry one through.

sentences.zh: 雖斟酌前史，備覩妍嗤，而愛嗜異情，取捨殊意，每含毫握簡，杼軸忘飡，終亦不足與班、左並馳，董、南齊轡。

translations.literal: Although I have weighed the earlier histories and seen their beauties and faults in full, yet because loves and hates differ, my choices and rejections differ in intent; each time I hold the brush and grasp the slip, the loom turns and I forget my meal—yet in the end I am still not equal to racing with Ban and Zuo, or matching reins with Dong and Nan.
translations.idiomatic: Though I have studied earlier histories and seen their strengths and flaws, personal taste shapes every choice. Again and again I take up brush and slip and forget to eat at the loom—yet I still cannot keep pace with Ban Gu and Sima Qian, or run even with Dong and Nan.

sentences.zh: 庶為後之君子削藳而已焉。

translations.literal: I can only hope to offer later gentlemen material to trim.
translations.idiomatic: I can only offer later readers something to cut and reshape for themselves.

sentences.zh: 黃帝使伶倫自大夏之西，阮隃之陰，取竹之嶰谷生，其竅厚均者，斷兩節間而吹之，以為黃鍾之宮。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor sent Ling Lun west of Great Xia, to the north of Mount Wanqu, to take bamboo from Xie Valley that grew with even bore and thickness, cut the space between two nodes, and blow it to make the note of the Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor sent Ling Lun west beyond Great Xia, to the northern side of Mount Wanqu, to take bamboo from Xie Valley with even bore and wall, cut between two nodes, and blow it to establish the Yellow Bell as the fundamental pitch.

sentences.zh: 制十二管，以聽鳳鳴，以定律呂。

translations.literal: He fashioned twelve tubes to listen to the phoenixes' cries and thereby fix the pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: He then made twelve pipes, listened to the phoenixes' cries, and fixed the standards of pitch.

sentences.zh: 夫聲有清濁，故協以宮商；

translations.literal: Sound has clear and murky qualities; therefore it is harmonized by gong and shang.
translations.idiomatic: Because sound has clear and murky tones, it is harmonized through gong and shang.

sentences.zh: 形有長短，故檢以丈尺；

translations.literal: Form has long and short measures; therefore it is tested by the foot and the yard.
translations.idiomatic: Because form has length and brevity, it is measured by foot and yard.

sentences.zh: 器有大小，故定以斛斗；

translations.literal: Vessels have large and small capacity; therefore they are fixed by the hu and the dou.
translations.idiomatic: Because vessels differ in size, they are fixed by the hu and the dou.

sentences.zh: 質有輕重，故平以鈞石。

translations.literal: Mass has light and heavy weight; therefore it is balanced by the jun and the stone.
translations.idiomatic: Because mass differs in weight, it is balanced by the jun and the stone.

sentences.zh: 故虞書曰：「乃同律、度、量、衡。

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents of Yu says: 'Thus unify pitch pipes, measures, quantities, and balances.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Documents of Yu says: 'Thus unify pitch pipes, length measures, capacity measures, and balances.'

sentences.zh: 」然則律呂，宮商之所由生也。

translations.literal: Thus pitch pipes are what give birth to gong and shang.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch pipes, then, are what give rise to the modes of gong and shang.

sentences.zh: 夫樂有器有文，有情有官。

translations.literal: Music has instruments and pattern, emotion and office.
translations.idiomatic: Music possesses instruments and pattern, feeling and function.

sentences.zh: 鍾鼓干戚，樂之器也；

translations.literal: Bells, drums, shields, and axes are the instruments of music;
translations.idiomatic: Bells, drums, shields, and axes are music's instruments;

sentences.zh: 屈伸舒疾，樂之文也；

translations.literal: bending, stretching, quickening, and slowing are music's pattern;
translations.idiomatic: bending, stretching, hastening, and slowing are its pattern;

sentences.zh: 「論倫無患，樂之情也；

translations.literal: 'discussing order without harm is the feeling of music;
translations.idiomatic: 'to discuss harmony without injury is music's inner feeling;

sentences.zh: 欣喜歡愛，樂之官也。

translations.literal: joy, delight, and love are music's offices.'
translations.idiomatic: joy, delight, and affection are its offices.'

sentences.zh: 」「是以君子反情以和志，廣樂以成教，故能情深而文明，氣盛而化神，和順積中，而英華發外。

translations.literal: 'Therefore the gentleman returns to true feeling to harmonize his will, extends music to complete his teaching, and so can make feeling deep and pattern luminous, breath strong and transformation numinous; harmony accumulates within, and splendor issues without.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Therefore the gentleman turns feeling back upon itself to harmonize the will, extends music to complete instruction, makes feeling deep and pattern bright, breath strong and transformation numinous; harmony gathers within, and splendor shines without.'

sentences.zh: 」故曰：「樂者，心之動也；

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: 'Music is the movement of the heart;
translations.idiomatic: Hence it is said: 'Music is the movement of the heart;

sentences.zh: 聲者，樂之象也。

translations.literal: sound is the image of music.'
translations.idiomatic: sound is the image of music.'

sentences.zh: 」周禮曰：「乃奏黃鍾，歌大呂，舞雲門，以祀天神。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou says: 'Then play the Yellow Bell, sing the Great Lu, and dance the Cloud Gate to sacrifice to the Heavenly Spirit.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou says: 'Then play the Yellow Bell, sing the Great Lu, and dance the Cloud Gate to sacrifice to the Heavenly Spirit.'

sentences.zh: 乃奏太蔟，歌應鍾，舞咸池，以祭地祇。

translations.literal: Then play the Great Cu, sing the Responding Bell, and dance the Xian Pool to sacrifice to the Earthly Spirits.'
translations.idiomatic: Then play the Great Cu, sing the Responding Bell, and dance the Xian Pool to sacrifice to the Earthly Spirits.'

sentences.zh: 」四望山川先祖，各有其樂。

translations.literal: The four [sacrifices to] outlooks, mountains, rivers, and ancestors each had its own music.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices to the four outlooks, mountains, rivers, and ancestors each had its proper music.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「圜鍾為宮，黃鍾為角，太蔟為徵，[1]姑洗為羽，雷鼓雷鼗，孤竹之管，雲和之琴瑟，雲門之舞，冬日至，於地上之圜丘奏之。

translations.literal: It also says: 'The round bell serves as gong, the Yellow Bell as jue, the Great Cu as zhi, [1] the Gu Xian as yu; thunder drums and thunder tambourines, pipes of solitary bamboo, qin and se of Yunhe, and the dance of the Cloud Gate—at the winter solstice they are performed at the round mound altar on earth.'
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 'The round bell serves as gong, the Yellow Bell as jue, the Great Cu as zhi, [1] the Gu Xian as yu; with thunder drums and thunder tambourines, pipes of solitary bamboo, Yunhe qin and se, and the Cloud Gate dance—at the winter solstice these are performed at the round altar on earth.'

sentences.zh: 若樂六變，則天神皆降，可得而禮矣。

translations.literal: If the six changes of music are performed, then the spirits of Heaven all descend and can be received in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When the six musical changes are performed, the heavenly spirits descend and may be received in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」地祇人鬼，禮亦如之。

translations.literal: Earthly spirits and human ghosts were treated in ritual in the same way.
translations.idiomatic: Earthly spirits and human ghosts were honored by the same ritual logic.

sentences.zh: 其可以感物興化，若此之深也。

translations.literal: That it can move things and transform customs to this depth is clear.
translations.idiomatic: That music can move things and transform customs to such depth is evident.

sentences.zh: 「道始於一，一生二，二生三，三三而九。

translations.literal: 'The Way begins in One; One gives birth to Two, Two gives birth to Three, and three threes make nine.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The Way begins in One; One engenders Two, Two engenders Three, and three threes make nine.'

sentences.zh: [2]故黃鍾之數六，分而為雌雄十二鍾。

translations.literal: [2] Therefore the number of the Yellow Bell is six; divided, it becomes the twelve male and female bells.
translations.idiomatic: [2] The number of the Yellow Bell is six; divided, it yields the twelve male and female pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 鍾以三成，故置一而三之，凡積分十七萬七千一百四十七，為黃鍾之實。

translations.literal: The bell is completed by threefold increase; therefore set one and triple it—altogether accumulating a fraction of one hundred seventy-seven thousand one hundred forty-seven as the full measure of the Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Each pipe is built by tripling; set one and triple it repeatedly until the accumulated fraction reaches 177,147 as the full measure of the Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 故黃鍾位子，主十一月，下生林鍾。

translations.literal: Therefore the Yellow Bell occupies the zi position and governs the eleventh month; from it the Lin Bell is generated downward.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Bell stands in the zi position and governs the eleventh month; from it the Lin Bell is generated downward.

sentences.zh: 林鍾之數五十四，主六月，上生太蔟。

translations.literal: The number of the Lin Bell is fifty-four; it governs the sixth month; upward from it the Great Cu is generated.
translations.idiomatic: The Lin Bell's number is fifty-four; it governs the sixth month; upward from it comes the Great Cu.

sentences.zh: 太蔟之數七十二，主正月，下生南呂。

translations.literal: The number of the Great Cu is seventy-two; it governs the first month; downward from it the Southern Lu is generated.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Cu's number is seventy-two; it governs the first month; downward from it comes the Southern Lu.

sentences.zh: 南呂之數四十八，主八月，上生姑洗。

translations.literal: The number of the Southern Lu is forty-eight; it governs the eighth month; upward from it the Gu Xian is generated.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Lu's number is forty-eight; it governs the eighth month; upward from it comes the Gu Xian.

sentences.zh: 姑洗之數六十四，主三月，下生應鍾。

translations.literal: The number of the Gu Xian is sixty-four; it governs the third month; downward from it the Responding Bell is generated.
translations.idiomatic: The Gu Xian's number is sixty-four; it governs the third month; downward from it comes the Responding Bell.

sentences.zh: 應鍾之數四十三，主十月，上生蕤賓。

translations.literal: The number of the Responding Bell is forty-three; it governs the tenth month; upward from it the Flaccid Guest is generated.
translations.idiomatic: The Responding Bell's number is forty-three; it governs the tenth month; upward from it comes the Flaccid Guest.

sentences.zh: 蕤賓之數五十七，主五月，上生大呂。

translations.literal: The number of the Flaccid Guest is fifty-seven; it governs the fifth month; upward from it the Great Lu is generated.
translations.idiomatic: The Flaccid Guest's number is fifty-seven; it governs the fifth month; upward from it comes the Great Lu.

sentences.zh: 大呂之數七十六，主十二月，下生夷則。

translations.literal: The number of the Great Lu is seventy-six; it governs the twelfth month; downward from it the Leveling Ze is generated.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Lu's number is seventy-six; it governs the twelfth month; downward from it comes the Leveling Ze.

sentences.zh: 夷則之數五十一，[3]主七月，上生夾鍾。

translations.literal: The number of the Leveling Ze is fifty-one, [3] governing the seventh month; upward from it the Pinched Bell is generated.
translations.idiomatic: The Leveling Ze's number is fifty-one, [3] governing the seventh month; upward from it comes the Pinched Bell.

sentences.zh: 夾鍾之數六十七，主二月，下生無射。

translations.literal: The number of the Pinched Bell is sixty-seven; it governs the second month; downward from it the Untempered Pitch is generated.
translations.idiomatic: The Pinched Bell's number is sixty-seven; it governs the second month; downward from it comes the Untempered Pitch.

sentences.zh: 無射之數四十五，主九月，上生中呂。

translations.literal: The number of the Untempered Pitch is forty-five; it governs the ninth month; upward from it the Middle Lu is generated.
translations.idiomatic: The Untempered Pitch's number is forty-five; it governs the ninth month; upward from it comes the Middle Lu.

sentences.zh: 中呂之數六十，主四月，極不生。

translations.literal: The number of the Middle Lu is sixty; it governs the fourth month; at the extreme, no further generation occurs.
translations.idiomatic: The Middle Lu's number is sixty; it governs the fourth month; at the extreme, no further generation occurs.

sentences.zh: 〈極不生，鍾律不能復相生。〉

translations.literal: 〈At the extreme no generation occurs; the pitch pipes cannot again generate one another.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈At the extreme no further generation occurs; the pitch pipes cannot generate one another again.〉

sentences.zh: 宮生徵，徵生商，商生羽，羽生角，角生姑洗，姑洗生應鍾，比於正音，故為和。

translations.literal: Gong generates zhi, zhi generates shang, shang generates yu, yu generates jue; jue generates Gu Xian, Gu Xian generates Responding Bell—compared with the correct pitches, therefore they are harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Gong generates zhi, zhi generates shang, shang generates yu, yu generates jue; jue generates Gu Xian, and Gu Xian generates Responding Bell. Compared with the correct pitches, these form harmony.

translations.literal: [4] (Editorial note.)
translations.idiomatic: [4] (Editorial note.)

sentences.zh: 〈姑洗三月，應鍾十月，與正音比，故為和。

translations.literal: 〈Gu Xian is the third month and Responding Bell the tenth month; compared with the correct pitches, therefore they are harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Gu Xian corresponds to the third month and Responding Bell to the tenth month; compared with the correct pitches, they form harmony.

sentences.zh: 和，從聲也。〉

translations.literal: Harmony is a following sound.〉
translations.idiomatic: Harmony is a following tone.〉

sentences.zh: [5]應鍾生蕤賓，蕤賓不比於正音，故為繆。

translations.literal: [5] Responding Bell generates Flaccid Guest; Flaccid Guest is not compared with the correct pitch, therefore it is dissonant.
translations.idiomatic: [5] Responding Bell generates Flaccid Guest; Flaccid Guest does not match the correct pitch, and therefore is dissonant.

sentences.zh: 〈繆，音相干也。

translations.literal: 〈Dissonance means that the tones interfere with one another.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Dissonance means the tones interfere with one another.

sentences.zh: 周律故有繆、和，為武王伐紂七音也。〉

translations.literal: The pitch standards of Zhou therefore had dissonance and harmony, being the seven tones for King Wu's campaign against Zhou.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou pitch standards thus included dissonant and harmonious tones—the seven tones used when King Wu campaigned against the Tyrant of Shang.〉

sentences.zh: 日冬至，音比林鍾浸以濁；

translations.literal: At the winter solstice, the tone compares with the Lin Bell and gradually becomes murky;
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice the tone aligns with the Lin Bell and gradually grows murky;

sentences.zh: 日夏至，音比黃鍾浸以清。

translations.literal: at the summer solstice, the tone compares with the Yellow Bell and gradually becomes clear.
translations.idiomatic: at the summer solstice it aligns with the Yellow Bell and gradually grows clear.

sentences.zh: 以十二月律應二十四時。

translations.literal: The twelve monthly pitch standards correspond to the twenty-four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve monthly pitch pipes correspond to the twenty-four seasonal nodes.

sentences.zh: 甲子，中呂之徵也；

translations.literal: The jiazi day is the zhi of the Middle Lu;
translations.idiomatic: The jiazi day is the zhi-tone of Middle Lu;

sentences.zh: 丙子，夾鍾之羽也；

translations.literal: the bingzi day is the yu of the Pinched Bell;
translations.idiomatic: the bingzi day is the yu-tone of the Pinched Bell;

sentences.zh: 戊子，黃鍾之宮也；

translations.literal: the wuzi day is the gong of the Yellow Bell;
translations.idiomatic: the wuzi day is the gong-tone of the Yellow Bell;

sentences.zh: 庚子，無射之商也；

translations.literal: the gengzi day is the shang of the Untempered Pitch;
translations.idiomatic: the gengzi day is the shang-tone of the Untempered Pitch;

sentences.zh: 壬子，夷則之角也。」

translations.literal: the renzi day is the jue of the Leveling Ze.」
translations.idiomatic: the renzi day is the jue-tone of the Leveling Ze.」

sentences.zh: 「古人為度量輕重，皆生乎天道。

translations.literal: 「The ancients, in making measures of weight and lightness, all derived them from the Way of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 「In establishing measures of weight, the ancients all derived them from Heaven's way.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾之律長九寸，物以三生，三三九，三九二十七，故幅廣二尺七寸，古之制也。

translations.literal: The pitch standard of the Yellow Bell is nine inches long; things are generated by threes—three threes are nine, three nines twenty-seven—therefore the breadth of cloth is two feet seven inches; such was the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Bell pipe is nine inches long. Things are born by threes: three threes make nine, three nines twenty-seven—hence cloth was two feet seven inches wide in the ancient system.

sentences.zh: 音以八相生，故人長八尺，尋自倍，故八尺而為尋。

translations.literal: Tones are generated by eights; therefore a man's height is eight feet. The xun doubles itself; therefore eight feet make one xun.
translations.idiomatic: Because tones are generated by eights, a man's height is eight feet. The xun doubles upon itself, so eight feet make one xun.

sentences.zh: 有形即有聲，音之數五，以五乘八，五八四十尺為匹。

translations.literal: Where there is form there is sound; the number of tones is five; multiplying five by eight, five eights forty feet make one bolt.
translations.idiomatic: Form gives rise to sound. Tones number five; five times eight is forty feet, which makes one bolt of cloth.

sentences.zh: 匹者，中人之度也，一匹為制。

translations.literal: A bolt is the measure of an average man; one bolt was the standard.
translations.idiomatic: A bolt was the measure of an ordinary man and served as the standard length.

sentences.zh: 秋分而禾䅺定，

translations.literal: At the autumn equinox the grain awns are set,
translations.idiomatic: At the autumn equinox the grain awns are fixed,

sentences.zh: 〈䅺，禾穗芒也。〉

translations.literal: 〈The awn is the beard of the grain ear.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The awn is the bristle of the grain ear.〉

sentences.zh: 䅺定而禾孰。

translations.literal: when the awns are set, the grain ripens.
translations.idiomatic: and when the awns are set the grain ripens.

sentences.zh: 律之數十二，故十二䅺而當一粟，十二粟而當一寸。

translations.literal: The number of pitch standards is twelve; therefore twelve awns equal one grain, and twelve grains equal one inch.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch standards number twelve, so twelve awns equal one grain and twelve grains equal one inch.

sentences.zh: [6]律以當辰，音以當日。

translations.literal: [6] Pitch standards correspond to the chronograms; tones correspond to days.
translations.idiomatic: [6] Pitch standards correspond to the chronograms; tones correspond to days.

sentences.zh: 日之數十，故十寸而為尺，十尺為丈。

translations.literal: The number of days is ten; therefore ten inches make one foot, and ten feet one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Days number ten, so ten inches make a foot and ten feet a zhang.

sentences.zh: 其以為重，十二粟而當一分，十二分而當一銖，十二銖而當半兩。

translations.literal: As for weight, twelve grains equal one fen, twelve fen one zhu, and twelve zhu half a liang.
translations.idiomatic: For weight, twelve grains make one fen, twelve fen one zhu, and twelve zhu half a liang.

sentences.zh: 衡有左右，因而倍之，故二十四銖而當一兩。

translations.literal: The balance has left and right; therefore doubling it, twenty-four zhu equal one liang.
translations.idiomatic: The balance has left and right pans; doubled, twenty-four zhu make one liang.

sentences.zh: 天有四時，以成一歲，因而四之，四四十六，故十六兩而一斤。

translations.literal: Heaven has four seasons to complete one year; therefore multiplying by four, four fours sixteen, so sixteen liang make one jin.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has four seasons to complete a year; multiply by four and four fours make sixteen, so sixteen liang make one jin.

sentences.zh: 三月而一時，三十日一月，故三十斤而為一鈞。

translations.literal: Three months make one season, thirty days one month; therefore thirty jin make one jun.
translations.idiomatic: Three months make a season and thirty days a month, so thirty jin make one jun.

sentences.zh: 四時而一歲，故四鈞而一石。

translations.literal: Four seasons make one year; therefore four jun make one shi.
translations.idiomatic: Four seasons make a year, so four jun make one shi.

sentences.zh: 」「其為音也，一律而生五音，十二律而為六十音；

translations.literal: 」「As for sound, one pitch standard generates five tones; twelve pitch standards make sixty tones;
translations.idiomatic: 」「In sound, one pitch standard generates five tones; twelve standards yield sixty tones;

sentences.zh: 因而六之，六六三十六，故三百六十音以當一歲之日。

translations.literal: multiplying further by six, six sixes thirty-six, therefore three hundred sixty tones correspond to the days of one year.
translations.idiomatic: multiply by six and six sixes make thirty-six, so three hundred sixty tones match the days of a year.

sentences.zh: 故律曆之數，天地之道也。

translations.literal: Therefore the numbers of pitch pipes and the calendar are the Way of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the numbers of pitch pipes and the calendar embody the way of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 下生者倍，以三除之；

translations.literal: For downward generation, double and divide by three;
translations.idiomatic: In downward generation, double and divide by three;

sentences.zh: 上生者四，以三除之。」

translations.literal: for upward generation, multiply by four and divide by three.」
translations.idiomatic: in upward generation, multiply by four and divide by three.」

sentences.zh: 揚子雲曰：「聲生於日，

translations.literal: Yang Xiong said: 「Sound is born from the day,
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong said: 「Sound is born from the day,

sentences.zh: 〈謂甲己為角，乙庚為商，丙辛為徵，丁壬為羽，戊癸為宮。〉

translations.literal: 〈This means jia and ji are jue, yi and geng are shang, bing and xin are zhi, ding and ren are yu, and wu and gui are gong.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈That is, jia-ji days produce jue, yi-geng shang, bing-xin zhi, ding-ren yu, and wu-gui gong.〉

sentences.zh: 律生於辰，

translations.literal: pitch standards are born from the chronograms,
translations.idiomatic: pitch standards are born from the chronograms,

sentences.zh: 〈謂子為黃鍾，丑為大呂之屬。〉

translations.literal: 〈This means zi is the Yellow Bell, chou belongs to the Great Lu, and so on.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈That is, zi is the Yellow Bell, chou the Great Lu, and so forth.〉

sentences.zh: 聲以情質，

translations.literal: sound takes feeling as its substance,
translations.idiomatic: sound takes feeling as its substance,

sentences.zh: 〈質，正也。

translations.literal: 〈Substance means correctness.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Substance means correctness.

sentences.zh: 各以其行本情為正也。〉

translations.literal: Each takes the native disposition of its phase as correct.〉
translations.idiomatic: Each mode takes the native character of its phase as the standard.〉

sentences.zh: 律以和聲，

translations.literal: pitch standards harmonize sound,
translations.idiomatic: pitch standards harmonize sound,

sentences.zh: 〈當以律管鍾均，和其清濁之聲。〉

translations.literal: 〈One should use pitch pipes and bell standards to harmonize their clear and murky tones.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈One matches clear and murky tones with pitch pipes and bell standards.〉

sentences.zh: 聲律相協，而八音生。

translations.literal: When sound and pitch standards accord, the eight classes of tone are born.
translations.idiomatic: When sound and pitch standards accord, the eight classes of tone arise.

translations.literal: 〈Accord means harmony.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Accord means harmony.〉

sentences.zh: 宮、商、角、徵、羽，謂之五聲。

translations.literal: Gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu are called the five tones.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu are called the five tones.

sentences.zh: 金、石、匏、革、絲、竹、土、木，謂之八音。

translations.literal: Metal, stone, gourd, hide, silk, bamboo, earth, and wood are called the eight materials of sound.
translations.idiomatic: Metal, stone, gourd, hide, silk, bamboo, earth, and wood are called the eight materials of sound.

sentences.zh: 聲和音諧，是謂五樂。」

translations.literal: When sound and tone are harmonious, this is called the five kinds of music.」
translations.idiomatic: When sound and tone are in harmony, this is called the five kinds of music.」

sentences.zh: 夫陰陽和則景至，律氣應則灰除。

translations.literal: When yin and yang are in harmony, the shadow arrives; when pitch-breath responds, the ash is expelled.
translations.idiomatic: When yin and yang are in harmony the shadow is cast; when pitch-breath responds the ash is expelled.

sentences.zh: 是故天子常以冬夏至御前殿，合八能之士，陳八音，聽樂均，度晷景，候鍾律，權土炭，効陰陽。

translations.literal: Therefore the Son of Heaven regularly at the winter and summer solstices attends the front hall, assembles masters of the eight skills, arrays the eight tones, listens to the musical balance, measures the gnomon shadow, observes the pitch standards, weighs the charcoal and earth, and tests yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at the winter and summer solstices the Son of Heaven would attend the front hall, gather masters of the eight skills, array the eight tones, listen to the musical balance, measure the gnomon shadow, observe pitch standards, weigh charcoal and earth, and test yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 冬至陽氣應，則樂均清，景長極，黃鍾通，土炭輕而衡仰。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice yang-breath responds; then the musical balance is clear, the shadow longest, the Yellow Bell passes through, and the charcoal and earth are light while the balance tilts up.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice yang-breath responds: the balance sounds clear, the shadow reaches its maximum, the Yellow Bell pipe is active, and the charcoal and earth are light while the balance arm rises.

sentences.zh: [7]夏至陰氣應，則樂均濁，景短極，蕤賓通，土炭重而衡低。

translations.literal: [7] At the summer solstice yin-breath responds; then the musical balance is murky, the shadow shortest, the Flaccid Guest passes through, and the charcoal and earth are heavy while the balance tilts down.
translations.idiomatic: [7] At the summer solstice yin-breath responds: the balance sounds murky, the shadow is shortest, the Flaccid Guest pipe is active, and the charcoal and earth are heavy while the balance arm falls.

sentences.zh: 進退於先後五日之中，八能各以候狀聞。

translations.literal: Advancing and retreating within the five days before and after, each of the eight skills reports its observations according to condition.
translations.idiomatic: Within the five days before and after each solstice, each of the eight skills reports what it has observed.

sentences.zh: 太史令封上。

translations.literal: The Grand Astrologer seals and submits them upward.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Astrologer seals and submits the reports.

sentences.zh: 効則和，否則占。

translations.literal: If they accord, there is harmony; if not, prognostication is made.
translations.idiomatic: When the signs accord, all is harmonious; when they do not, divination follows.

sentences.zh: 候氣之法，為室三重，戶閉，塗釁周密，布緹幔。

translations.literal: The method of observing breath: build a chamber of three layers, close the doors, plaster it tightly and densely, and hang fine silk curtains.
translations.idiomatic: The method for observing qi: construct a triple chamber, close the doors, seal the walls tightly, and hang fine silk curtains.

sentences.zh: 室中以木為案，每律各一，內庳外高，從其方位，加律其上。

translations.literal: Inside the chamber place a wooden stand; for each pitch standard one stand, low within and high without, following its directional position, with the pitch standard placed upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Inside, set a wooden stand for each pitch standard—lower within, higher without—placed according to its direction with the standard pipe set on top.

sentences.zh: 以葭莩灰布其內端，案曆而候之。

translations.literal: Pack reed-fluff ash at the inner end and observe according to the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Pack reed-fluff ash at the inner end and observe according to the calendar.

sentences.zh: 氣至者灰動。

translations.literal: When the breath arrives, the ash moves.
translations.idiomatic: When qi arrives, the ash stirs.

sentences.zh: 其為氣動者其灰散，人及風所動者，其灰聚。

translations.literal: When it is breath that moves it, the ash scatters; when people or wind move it, the ash gathers.
translations.idiomatic: If qi moves it the ash scatters; if people or wind move it the ash clumps.

sentences.zh: [8]殿中候，用玉律十二。

translations.literal: [8] For observation within the palace, twelve jade pitch standards were used.
translations.idiomatic: [8] Observations within the palace used twelve jade pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 唯二至乃候靈臺，用竹律六十。

translations.literal: Only at the two solstices was the Spirit Terrace observed, using sixty bamboo pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the two solstices was the Spirit Terrace used, with sixty bamboo pitch standards.

sentences.zh: [9]取弘農宜陽縣金門山竹為管，河內葭莩為灰。

translations.literal: [9] Bamboo tubes were taken from Golden Gate Mountain in Yiyang county, Hongnong, and reed-fluff from the interior of the Yellow River for ash.
translations.idiomatic: [9] Bamboo tubes came from Golden Gate Mountain in Yiyang county, Hongnong; ash came from reed-fluff of the interior marshes.

translations.literal: [10] (Editorial note.)
translations.idiomatic: [10] (Editorial note.)

sentences.zh: 三代陵遲，音律失度。

translations.literal: The three dynasties declined, and pitch pipes and measures lost their standards.
translations.idiomatic: After the three dynasties declined, pitch pipes and measures lost their proper standards.

sentences.zh: 漢興，北平侯張蒼始定律曆。

translations.literal: When Han arose, Marquis Zhang of Beiping first fixed the pitch pipes and calendar.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han arose, Marquis Zhang of Beiping first established pitch pipes and the calendar.

sentences.zh: 孝武之世，置協律之官。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Wu, offices for harmonizing pitch standards were established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu offices were created to harmonize pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 元帝時，郎中京房知五音六十律之數，受學於小黃令焦延壽。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Yuan, the palace gentleman Jing Fang knew the numbers of the five tones and sixty pitch standards and received instruction from the Director of the Yellow Gate, Jiao Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yuan the palace gentleman Jing Fang mastered the five tones and sixty pitch standards, studying under Director Jiao Yanshou of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 其下生、上生，終於中呂，而十二律畢矣。

translations.literal: His downward and upward generation ended at the Middle Lu, and the twelve pitch standards were complete.
translations.idiomatic: His downward and upward generation ended at Middle Lu, completing the twelve pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 中呂上生執始，執始下生去滅，終於南事，而六十律畢矣。

translations.literal: From Middle Lu upward came Zhi Shi; from Zhi Shi downward came Qu Mie, ending at Southern Affairs—and the sixty pitch standards were complete.
translations.idiomatic: From Middle Lu upward came Zhi Shi; from Zhi Shi downward Qu Mie; ending at Southern Affairs—and the sixty pitch standards were complete.

sentences.zh: 夫十二律之變至於六十，猶八卦之變至於六十四也。

translations.literal: The transformation of the twelve pitch standards to sixty is like the transformation of the eight trigrams to sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: The extension of twelve pitch standards to sixty parallels the extension of the eight trigrams to sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 宓羲作易，紀陽氣之初，以為律法。

translations.literal: Fu Xi made the Changes, recording the beginning of yang-breath, and took it as the law of pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi created the Changes, marking the beginning of yang-breath, and made it the basis of pitch law.

sentences.zh: 建日冬至之聲，以黃鍾為宮，太蔟為商，姑洗為角，林鍾為徵，南呂為羽，應鍾為變宮，蕤賓為變徵。

translations.literal: Establishing the sound of the winter-solstice day, he took the Yellow Bell as gong, the Great Cu as shang, the Gu Xian as jue, the Lin Bell as zhi, the Southern Lu as yu, the Responding Bell as the altered gong, and the Flaccid Guest as the altered zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the winter-solstice tone as foundation, he set Yellow Bell as gong, Great Cu as shang, Gu Xian as jue, Lin Bell as zhi, Southern Lu as yu, Responding Bell as altered gong, and Flaccid Guest as altered zhi.

sentences.zh: 此聲氣之元，五音之正也。

translations.literal: This is the origin of breath-sound and the correctness of the five tones.
translations.idiomatic: This is the root of breath-sound and the true foundation of the five tones.

sentences.zh: 故各統一日。

translations.literal: Therefore each governs one day.
translations.idiomatic: Each therefore governs one day.

sentences.zh: 其餘以次運行，當日者各自為宮，而商角徵羽以類從焉。

translations.literal: The rest run in sequence; whichever day is current becomes gong for that day, while shang, jue, zhi, and yu follow by category.
translations.idiomatic: The rest follow in sequence: whichever day is current serves as gong, with shang, jue, zhi, and yu arranged by kind.

sentences.zh: 禮運篇曰：「五聲、六律、十二管還相為宮。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites says: 「The five tones, six pitch standards, and twelve pipes revolve to serve as one another's gong.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says: 「The five tones, six pitch standards, and twelve pipes rotate to serve as one another's gong.

sentences.zh: 」此之謂也。

translations.literal: 」This is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: 」This is what is meant.

sentences.zh: 以六十律分一朞之日，黃鍾自冬至始，及冬至而復，陰陽寒煖風雨之占於是生焉。

translations.literal: Dividing the days of one cycle by the sixty pitch standards, the Yellow Bell begins from the winter solstice and returns at the winter solstice; prognostications of yin and yang, cold and warm, wind and rain are thereby generated.
translations.idiomatic: Dividing the days of a cycle among sixty pitch standards, the Yellow Bell begins at the winter solstice and returns at winter solstice; from this arise forecasts of yin and yang, cold and warmth, wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 房又曰：「竹聲不可以度調，故作準以定數。

translations.literal: Fang also said: 「Bamboo sound cannot be used to measure tuning; therefore he made the pitch-standard instrument to fix the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Fang also said: 「Bamboo sound cannot fix tuning by itself, so he made the pitch-standard instrument to establish the numbers.

sentences.zh: 準之狀如瑟，長丈而十三弦，隱間九尺，以應黃鍾之律九寸；

translations.literal: The instrument's form is like a se, one zhang long with thirteen strings; the hidden space is nine feet, corresponding to the nine inches of the Yellow Bell pitch standard;
translations.idiomatic: The instrument resembles a se, one zhang long with thirteen strings; the hidden interval is nine feet, matching the Yellow Bell's nine inches;

sentences.zh: 中央一弦，下有畫分寸，以為六十律清濁之節。

translations.literal: on the central string below are marked inches and fen, serving as the gradations of clear and murky for the sixty pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: beneath the central string are marked inches and fen as gradations for the clear and murky levels of the sixty pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 」房言律詳於歆所奏，[11]其術施行於史官，候部用之。

translations.literal: 」Fang said that pitch standards were more detailed than what Xin presented; [11] his method was practiced by the historiographers and used by the observation offices.
translations.idiomatic: 」Fang held that pitch theory was more detailed than Liu Xin's presentation; [11] his method was practiced by historiographers and used in the observation offices.

sentences.zh: 續漢志具載其律準度數。

translations.literal: The Continued Han Treatises fully record his pitch-standard measurements and numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The Continued Han Treatises record his pitch-standard measurements in full.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和元年，待詔候鍾律殷肜上言：「官無曉六十律以準調音者，故待詔嚴嵩具以準法教子男宣，願召宣補學官，主調樂器。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang of Han, the awaiting-edict observer of pitch standards Yin Hong submitted: 「In the offices there is no one who understands the sixty pitch standards for tuning instruments; therefore the awaiting-edict Yan Song fully taught his son Nan Xuan the standard method, and I ask that Xuan be summoned to supplement the learning office and take charge of tuning instruments.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe under Emperor Zhang, awaiting-edict pitch observer Yin Hong submitted: 「No one in office understands the sixty pitch standards for tuning instruments. Awaiting-edict Yan Song has fully taught his son Nan Xuan the standard method; I ask that Xuan be summoned to the learning office to take charge of tuning instruments.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「嵩子學審曉律，別其族，協其聲者，審試。

translations.literal: 」The edict said: 「If Song's son has truly mastered pitch standards, distinguishing their clans and harmonizing their sounds, test him carefully.
translations.idiomatic: 」The edict replied: 「If Song's son has truly mastered pitch standards, distinguishing their families and harmonizing their sounds, test him carefully.

sentences.zh: 不得依託父學，以聾為聰。

translations.literal: He must not rely on his father's learning and pass off deafness as hearing.
translations.idiomatic: He must not rely on his father's learning and pass off deafness as hearing.

sentences.zh: 聲微妙，獨非莫知，獨是莫曉，以律錯吹，能知命十二律不失一，乃為能傳嵩學耳。

translations.literal: Sound is subtle and fine; only the non-knowing do not know, only the non-understanding do not understand. Using pitch standards to blow wrongly, if he can know and not miss one of the twelve pitch standards, only then can he transmit Song's learning.
translations.idiomatic: Sound is subtle: only the tone-deaf cannot know it, only the untrained cannot grasp it. If, when pitch standards are used to test him by blowing, he can identify all twelve without missing one, only then may he transmit Song's art.

sentences.zh: 」試宣十二律，其二中，其四不中，其六不知何律，宣遂罷。

translations.literal: 」They tested Xuan on the twelve pitch standards: two he got right, four wrong, and six he did not know which pitch standard they were—Xuan was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: 」They tested Xuan on the twelve standards: two correct, four wrong, and six he could not identify at all—so Xuan was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 自此律家莫能為準。

translations.literal: From this time masters of pitch standards could no longer make the standard instrument.
translations.idiomatic: From that time onward no master of pitch standards could make the standard instrument.

sentences.zh: 靈帝熹平六年，東觀召典律者太子舍人張光等問準意。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xiping under Emperor Ling, the Eastern Pavilion summoned pitch specialists including the heir apparent's household attendant Zhang Guang to inquire about the standard instrument.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xiping under Emperor Ling, the Eastern Pavilion summoned pitch specialists including Zhang Guang, household attendant to the heir apparent, to inquire about the standard instrument.

sentences.zh: 光等不知。

translations.literal: Guang and the others did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and the others did not know.

sentences.zh: 歸閱舊藏，乃得其器，形制如房書，猶不能定其絃緩急。

translations.literal: Returning to examine the old repository, they then obtained the instrument; its form matched Fang's book, yet they still could not determine the tightness or slackness of its strings.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the old repository they found the instrument; its form matched Fang's description, yet they still could not determine how tight or slack the strings should be.

sentences.zh: 音不可書以曉人，[12]知之者欲教而無從，心達者體知而無師，故史官能辨清濁者遂絕。

translations.literal: Sound cannot be written to make people understand; [12] those who know wish to teach but have no one to teach, those whose hearts grasp it understand in the body but have no teacher—therefore those among historiographers who could distinguish clear and murky finally perished.
translations.idiomatic: Sound cannot be written down for others to understand; [12] those who know it wish to teach but find no pupils, those who grasp it inwardly have no master—so among historiographers the ability to distinguish clear from murky died out.

sentences.zh: 其可以相傳者，唯候氣而已。

translations.literal: What could be transmitted was only the observation of breath.
translations.idiomatic: What could still be handed down was only the method of observing qi.
