translations.idiomatic: Nine inches; fraction 174,762.

sentences.zh: 〈三分之二，不足二千三百八十四，三分之一〉

translations.literal: 〈Two-thirds; short by 2,384, one-third〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Two-thirds of the remainder; short by 2,384, plus one-third〉

sentences.zh: [24] 十七萬七千一百四十七

translations.idiomatic: [24] 177,147 (full Yellow Bell fraction).

sentences.zh: 論曰：律呂相生，皆三分而損益之。

translations.literal: Discussion says: Pitch pipes mutually generate one another, all by taking one-third and increasing or decreasing.
translations.idiomatic: The discussion states: pitch pipes generate one another by adding or subtracting one-third each time.

sentences.zh: 先儒推十二律，從子至亥，每三之，凡十七萬七千一百四十七，而三約之，是為上生。

translations.literal: Earlier scholars calculated the twelve pitch standards from zi to hai; tripling each time, altogether 177,147, and reducing by three—that is upward generation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars derived the twelve standards from zi to hai by tripling until they reached 177,147, then dividing by three for upward generation.

sentences.zh: 故漢志云：三分損一，下生林鍾，三分益一，上生太蔟。

translations.literal: Therefore the Han Treatises say: reducing by one-third downward generates the Lin Bell; increasing by one-third upward generates the Great Cu.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Han Treatises: subtract one-third downward to get Lin Bell; add one-third upward to get Great Cu.

sentences.zh: 無射既上生中呂，則中呂又當上生黃鍾，然後五聲、六律、十二管還相為宮。

translations.literal: Once Untempered Pitch upward generates Middle Lu, then Middle Lu should again upward generate Yellow Bell—only then do the five tones, six pitch standards, and twelve pipes revolve to serve as one another's gong.
translations.idiomatic: Once Untempered Pitch generates Middle Lu upward, Middle Lu should generate Yellow Bell upward—only then can the five tones, six standards, and twelve pipes rotate as one another's gong.

sentences.zh: 今上生不及黃鍾實二千三百八十四，九約實一千九百六十八為一分，此則不周九寸之律一分有奇，豈得還為宮乎？

translations.literal: Now upward generation falls short of the Yellow Bell's full measure by 2,384; reducing the full measure by nine leaves 1,968 as one fen—thus the pipe falls more than one fen short of nine inches. How can it return to serve as gong?
translations.idiomatic: Yet upward generation now falls 2,384 short of the Yellow Bell's full measure—more than one fen shy of nine inches. How can the cycle return to gong?

sentences.zh: 凡三分益一為上生，三分損一為下生，此其大略，猶周天斗分四分之一耳。

translations.literal: In general, increasing by one-third is upward generation; reducing by one-third is downward generation—this is the broad outline, like the quarter-day fraction in a full celestial circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Increasing by one-third is upward generation; decreasing by one-third is downward generation—the broad principle, comparable to the quarter-day fraction in a full celestial circuit.

sentences.zh: 京房不思此意，比十二律微有所增，方引而伸之，中呂上生執始，執始下生去滅，至于南事，為六十律，竟復不合，彌益其疏。

translations.literal: Jing Fang did not consider this meaning; comparing the twelve pitch standards, he slightly increased each, then extended them further—Middle Lu upward generating Zhi Shi, Zhi Shi downward generating Qu Mie, down to Southern Affairs for sixty pitch standards—yet in the end they still did not accord, only making the error worse.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang missed this point. Slightly enlarging each of the twelve standards and extending the series—Middle Lu to Zhi Shi, Zhi Shi to Qu Mie, down to Southern Affairs for sixty standards—he still could not close the cycle, only widening the error.

sentences.zh: 班氏所志，未能通律呂本源，徒訓角為觸，徵為祉，陽氣施種於黃鍾，如斯之屬，空煩其文，而為辭費。

translations.literal: What Ban's treatise records could not penetrate the root of pitch pipes and tones; he merely glossed jue as 'touch' and zhi as 'blessing,' saying yang-breath sows seed in the Yellow Bell—such items only clutter the text with empty words.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu's account never reached the root of pitch theory; he merely glossed jue as 'touch' and zhi as 'blessing,' or said yang-breath sows in the Yellow Bell—empty verbiage that burdens the text.

sentences.zh: 又推九六，欲符劉歆三統之數，假託非類，以飾其說，皆孟堅之妄矣。

translations.literal: He also pushed the numbers nine and six, wishing to match Liu Xin's numbers of the Three Systems, falsely borrowing unlike categories to adorn his doctrine—all Meng Jian's errors.
translations.idiomatic: He also forced the numbers nine and six to fit Liu Xin's Three Systems, borrowing unrelated categories to dress up his doctrine—all Ban Gu's mistakes.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕從朔方上書，云前漢志但載十二律，[25]不及六十。

translations.literal: Cai Yong, in a memorial from Shuofang, said that the Former Han Treatises recorded only the twelve pitch standards, [25] not reaching sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong wrote from Shuofang that the Former Han Treatises recorded only twelve pitch standards, [25] not sixty.

sentences.zh: 六律尺寸相生，司馬彪皆已志之。

translations.literal: The mutual generation of the six pitch standards by length—Sima Biao had already recorded them in his treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao had already recorded how the six standards generate one another by pipe length.

sentences.zh: 漢末，亡失雅樂，黃初中，鑄工柴玉巧有意思，形器之中，多所造作。

translations.literal: At the end of Han the refined music was lost; in the Huangchu era the casting artisan Chai Yu was clever and inventive, and among instruments he made many creations.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Han refined music was lost. In the Huangchu era the bell-caster Chai Yu was ingenious and produced many new instruments.

sentences.zh: 協律都尉杜夔令玉鑄鍾，其聲清濁，多不如法。

translations.literal: The Director of Harmonizing Pitch Standards Du Kui ordered Yu to cast bells; their clear and murky tones mostly did not match the law.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Harmonizing Pitch Standards Du Kui had Yu cast bells, but their clear and murky tones mostly failed to match the standard.

sentences.zh: 數毀改作，玉甚厭之，謂夔清濁任意。

translations.literal: Repeatedly destroyed and remade, Yu grew very weary of it, saying that Kui adjusted clear and murky at will.
translations.idiomatic: Yu remade them again and again until he grew weary, accusing Kui of adjusting clear and murky arbitrarily.

sentences.zh: 更相訴白於魏王。

translations.literal: They repeatedly accused one another before the King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They repeatedly brought accusations against each other before the King of Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏王取玉所鑄鍾，雜錯更試，然後知夔為精，於是罪玉及諸子，皆為養馬士。

translations.literal: The King of Wei took the bells Yu had cast, mixed and tested them further, and then knew that Kui was the expert; therefore he punished Yu and his sons, all becoming horse-keepers.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wei mixed and retested Yu's bells, then recognized Kui's mastery and punished Yu and his sons, reducing them all to horse-keepers.

translations.literal: [26] (Editorial note.)
translations.idiomatic: [26] (Editorial note.)

sentences.zh: 晉泰始十年，中書監荀勗、中書令張華，出御府銅竹律二十五具，部太樂郎劉秀等校試，其三具與杜夔及左延年律法同，其二十二具，視其銘題尺寸，是笛律也。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taishi of Jin, Palace Supervisor Xun Xu and Palace Secretary Zhang Hua produced twenty-five bronze and bamboo pitch standards from the imperial storehouse; Director of Music Liu Xiu and others tested them—three matched the pitch law of Du Kui and Zuo Yanian, while the other twenty-two, judging by their inscribed titles and dimensions, were flute standards.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Taishi year ten, Xun Xu and Zhang Hua brought out twenty-five bronze and bamboo standards from the imperial treasury for testing by Director of Music Liu Xiu and others. Three matched Du Kui's and Zuo Yanian's pitch law; the other twenty-two, by their inscriptions and dimensions, were flute standards.

sentences.zh: 問協律中郎將列和，辭：「昔魏明帝時，令和承受笛聲，以作此律，欲使學者別居一坊，歌詠講習，依此律調。

translations.literal: They questioned Director of Harmonizing Pitch Standards Lie He, who replied: 「In the time of Emperor Ming of Wei he ordered He to receive the flute sounds and make these standards, wishing that learners dwell in a separate ward, singing and practicing according to this pitch tuning.
translations.idiomatic: They questioned Lie He, Director of Harmonizing Pitch Standards, who replied: 「Under Emperor Ming of Wei I was ordered to take flute sound as the basis for these standards, so students might practice in a separate ward tuned to them.

sentences.zh: 至於都合樂時，但識其尺寸之名，則絲竹歌詠，皆得均合。

translations.literal: When assembling music at the capital, one need only know the names of the dimensions, and then silk, bamboo, song, and chant all achieve even blend.
translations.idiomatic: When music was assembled at court, knowing the dimension names alone allowed strings, bamboo, and voices to blend evenly.

sentences.zh: 歌聲濁者，用長笛長律；

translations.literal: For murky singing use the long flute and long standard;
translations.idiomatic: Murky voices used the long flute and long standard;

sentences.zh: 歌聲清者，用短笛短律。

translations.literal: for clear singing use the short flute and short standard.
translations.idiomatic: clear voices the short flute and short standard.

sentences.zh: 凡絃歌調張清濁之制，不依笛尺寸名之，則不可知也。」

translations.literal: In general the system for adjusting clear and murky in string-song tuning does not follow the flute's dimensional names, and then it cannot be known.」
translations.idiomatic: The system for adjusting clear and murky in string-song tuning depends on those flute dimension names—without them it cannot be known.」

sentences.zh: 勗等奏：「昔先王之作樂也，以振風蕩俗，饗神佑賢，[27]必協律呂之和，以節八音之中。

translations.literal: Xu and the others memorialized: 「When the former kings made music, it was to stir the wind and move custom, to feast the spirits and aid the worthy, [27] necessarily harmonizing the pitch pipes and tones to regulate the eight materials of sound.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and his colleagues memorialized: 「When the former kings made music, they stirred the wind and moved custom, feasted spirits and aided the worthy, [27] always harmonizing pitch pipes and tones to regulate the eight sounds.

sentences.zh: [28]是故郊祀朝宴，用之有制，歌奏分敍，清濁有宜。

translations.literal: [28] Therefore suburban sacrifice and court feast used it with rules; song and performance were divided in order, and clear and murky had their proper places.
translations.idiomatic: [28] Hence suburban sacrifice and court feast followed fixed rules; song and performance were ordered, clear and murky properly placed.

sentences.zh: 故曰『五聲十二律，還相為宮』。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said, 'The five tones and twelve pitch standards revolve to serve as one another's gong.'
translations.idiomatic: Thus the saying: 'The five tones and twelve standards revolve to serve as one another's gong.'

sentences.zh: 此經傳記籍可得而知者也。

translations.literal: This can be known from the classics, transmissions, records, and registers.
translations.idiomatic: This is known from the classics, transmissions, and historical records.

sentences.zh: 如和對辭，笛之長短，無所象則，率意而作，不由曲度。

translations.literal: As for He's reply, the flute's length and shortness have no model to imitate; he made them according to inclination, not following musical degree.
translations.idiomatic: He's reply shows that flute length had no model; he made them by inclination, not by musical degree.

sentences.zh: 考以正律，皆不相應，吹其聲均，多不諧合。

translations.literal: Tested against the correct pitch standards, none correspond; blow their sounds evenly and most do not harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Tested against correct pitch standards they do not correspond; blown evenly, most fail to harmonize.

sentences.zh: 又辭：『先師傳笛，別其清濁，直以長短，工人裁制，舊不依律。

translations.literal: He also said: 『The master transmitted the flute, distinguishing its clear and murky; he simply used length and shortness, and craftsmen cut them—of old they did not follow pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 『The master transmitted flutes by distinguishing clear and murky through length alone; craftsmen cut them by habit, never following pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 』是為作笛無法。

translations.literal: 』This is making flutes without method.
translations.idiomatic: 』That is making flutes without method.

sentences.zh: 而和寫笛造律，[29]又令琴瑟歌詠，從之為正，非所以稽古先哲，垂憲于後者也。

translations.literal: Yet He wrote down flutes to make pitch standards, [29] and further made zithers, se, and songs follow them as correct—this is not how to examine antiquity, consult the ancients, and hand down law to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Yet He wrote flutes into pitch law [29] and made zithers, se, and songs follow them as the standard—not the way to examine antiquity and hand down law to posterity.

sentences.zh: 謹條牒諸律，問和意狀如左。

translations.literal: We respectfully set forth the various pitch standards and question He's intent as follows.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully list the pitch standards and question He's intent as follows.

sentences.zh: 及依典制，用十二律造笛像十二枚，聲均調和，器用便利。

translations.literal: According to canonical system, use the twelve pitch standards to make twelve flutes modeled on the twelve; the sounds are evenly harmonized and the instruments convenient to use.
translations.idiomatic: By canonical system, twelve pitch standards should yield twelve flutes, one hole per standard, evenly tuned and convenient in use.

sentences.zh: 講肄彈擊，必合律呂，況乎宴饗萬國，奏之廟堂者哉！

translations.literal: In instruction and performance they must accord with pitch pipes and tones—how much more when feasting the ten thousand states and performing in the ancestral hall!
translations.idiomatic: In instruction and performance they must match pitch pipes and tones—how much more when feasting the myriad states in the ancestral hall!

sentences.zh: 雖伶、夔曠遠，至音難精，猶宜儀刑古昔，[30]以求厥衷，合于經禮，於制為詳。

translations.literal: Although Ling Lun and Kui are far off and ultimate tone is hard to perfect, one should still take the ancient as model, [30] seeking the central meaning, conforming to the classic rites—in regulation this is thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ling Lun and Kui are far away and perfect tone hard to attain, one should still model the ancients [30], seek the central meaning, and conform to the classic rites.

sentences.zh: 若可施用，請更部笛工，選竹造作，下太樂、樂府施行。

translations.literal: If this can be applied, please further assign flute craftsmen, select bamboo and make them, and have the Director of Music and Music Office put them into practice.
translations.idiomatic: If approved, assign flute craftsmen to select bamboo and make them, and order the Director of Music and Music Office to implement them.

sentences.zh: [31]平議諸杜夔、左延年律可皆留。

translations.literal: [31] The court discussion: the pitch standards of Du Kui and Zuo Yanian may all be retained.
translations.idiomatic: [31] The court discussion held that Du Kui's and Zuo Yanian's pitch standards should all be retained.

sentences.zh: 其御府笛正聲下徵各一具，皆銘題作者姓名。

translations.literal: Of the imperial-store flutes, one each for correct sound and lower zhi, all inscribed with the maker's name.
translations.idiomatic: Of the imperial flutes, one each for correct sound and lower zhi bore the maker's inscribed name.

sentences.zh: 其餘無所施用，還付御府毀。

translations.literal: The rest had no use and were returned to the imperial store for destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were useless and were returned to the imperial store for destruction.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: 」The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: 」The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 勗又問和：「作笛為可依十二律作十二笛，令一孔依一律，然後乃以為樂不？

translations.literal: Xu again questioned He: 「In making flutes, can one follow the twelve pitch standards to make twelve flutes, with one hole per standard—and only then make music?
translations.idiomatic: Xu questioned He again: 「Can flutes be made according to the twelve pitch standards, twelve flutes with one hole per standard—and only then serve as the basis of music?

sentences.zh: 」和辭：「太樂東廂長笛正聲已長四尺二寸，今當復取其下徵之聲；

translations.literal: 」He replied: 「The long flute of correct sound in the eastern wing of the Grand Music Office is already four feet two inches long; now we should again take the sound of the lower zhi;
translations.idiomatic: 」He replied: 「The eastern-wing long flute in correct sound is already four feet two inches; we must now take the lower-zhi tone as well;

sentences.zh: 於法，聲濁者笛當長，計其尺寸，乃五尺有餘，和昔日作之，不可吹也。

translations.literal: by method, murky sound requires a longer flute; calculating the dimension, it would be more than five feet—the flute He made in former days cannot be blown.
translations.idiomatic: by rule murky sound requires a longer pipe; by calculation it would exceed five feet—the flute He made before cannot be blown.

sentences.zh: 又笛諸孔，雖不校試，意謂不能得一孔輒應一律也。

translations.literal: Moreover, although the flute's holes were not tested and calibrated, in intent one could not have each hole respond to one pitch standard.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though the flute holes were never tested, it seems impossible that each hole could match one pitch standard.

sentences.zh: 」案太樂，四尺二寸笛正聲均應蕤賓，以十二律還相為宮，推法下徵之孔，當應律大呂。

translations.literal: 」Examining the Grand Music Office: a four-foot-two-inch flute in correct sound evenly responds to Flaccid Guest; taking the twelve pitch standards revolving as gong, the hole for lower zhi by calculation should respond to the Great Lu standard.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Grand Music Office found that a four-foot-two-inch flute in correct sound matches Flaccid Guest; by the twelve-standard cycle the lower-zhi hole should match Great Lu.

sentences.zh: 大呂笛長二尺六寸有奇，不得長五尺餘。

translations.literal: A Great Lu flute is a little more than two feet six inches long and cannot be more than five feet.
translations.idiomatic: A Great Lu flute is only a little over two feet six inches and cannot be five feet long.

sentences.zh: 令太樂郎劉秀、鄧昊等依律作大呂笛以示和。

translations.literal: They ordered the music officers Liu Xiu, Deng Hao, and others to make a Great Lu flute according to the pitch standards to show He.
translations.idiomatic: They ordered Liu Xiu, Deng Hao, and other music officers to make a Great Lu flute by the standards and show it to He.

sentences.zh: 又吹七律，一孔一校，聲皆相應。

translations.literal: Blowing the seven pitch standards, one hole tested for each, the sounds all corresponded.
translations.idiomatic: When each of the seven standards was tested at one hole, every sound corresponded.

sentences.zh: 然後令郝生鼓箏，宋同吹笛，以為雜引、相和諸曲。

translations.literal: Then they had Master Hao pluck the zheng and Song Tong blow the flute for miscellaneous preludes and harmony pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Then Master Hao played the zheng and Song Tong the flute on miscellaneous preludes and harmony pieces.

sentences.zh: 和乃辭曰：「自和父祖漢世以來，笛家相傳，不知此法，而今調均與律相應，實非所及也。

translations.literal: He then said: 「From my father and grandfather in Han times, flute masters transmitted their art without knowing this method; that the tuning now accords with the pitch standards is truly beyond my reach.
translations.idiomatic: He then said: 「Flute masters in my family since Han times never knew this method; that tuning now matches the standards is truly beyond me.

sentences.zh: 」郝生、魯基、种整、朱夏，皆與和同。

translations.literal: 」Master Hao, Lu Ji, Chong Zheng, and Zhu Xia all agreed with He.
translations.idiomatic: 」Hao, Lu Ji, Chong Zheng, and Zhu Xia all agreed with He.

sentences.zh: 又問和：「笛有六孔，及其體中之空為七。

translations.literal: They again questioned He: 「The flute has six holes, and the empty space within its body makes seven.
translations.idiomatic: They asked He again: 「A flute has six holes, and the hollow within makes seven.

sentences.zh: 和為能盡名其宮商角徵不？

translations.literal: Can He fully name their gong, shang, jue, zhi?
translations.idiomatic: Can you name every gong, shang, jue, and zhi?

sentences.zh: 孔調與不調，以何檢知？

translations.literal: Whether holes are in tune or not—by what is it tested and known?
translations.idiomatic: How can one test whether each hole is in tune?

sentences.zh: 」和辭：「先師相傳，吹笛但以作曲相語，為某曲當舉某指，[32]初不知七孔盡應何聲也。

translations.literal: 」He replied: 「The master transmitted that in blowing the flute one only speaks through composing pieces, saying for such a piece raise such a finger; [32] at first one did not know what sound all seven holes should produce.
translations.idiomatic: 」He replied: 「Masters taught only by pieces—'for this melody use this finger' [32]—without knowing what the seven holes should sound.

sentences.zh: 若當作笛，其仰尚方笛工，依案舊像訖，但吹取鳴者，初不復校其諸孔調與不調也。

translations.literal: If one were making a flute, one looked up to the imperial flute craftsmen, followed the old model to completion, but only blew to get a sounding note—at first one never again calibrated whether the various holes were in tune or not.
translations.idiomatic: When making a flute one copied the imperial craftsmen's old models and merely blew until it sounded, never calibrating the holes.

sentences.zh: 」案周禮調樂金石，有一定之聲，是故造鍾磬者，先依律調之，然後施於廂懸。

translations.literal: 」Examining the Rites of Zhou on tuning metal and stone for music: there are fixed sounds; therefore those who cast bells and chimes first tune them by pitch standards, then place them in the side-frame suspension.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Rites of Zhou require fixed tones for bells and stones; casters first tune by pitch standards, then hang them in the frame.

sentences.zh: 作樂之時，諸音皆受鍾磬之均，即為悉應律也。

translations.literal: When making music, all tones receive the evenness of bells and chimes and thereby all respond to the pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: In performance all tones take their evenness from bells and chimes and thus match the standards.

sentences.zh: 至於饗宴殿堂之上，無廂懸鍾磬，以笛有一定調，故諸絃歌皆從笛為正。

translations.literal: In feasts in the hall above, without side-frame bells and chimes, because the flute has a fixed tuning, all string songs follow the flute as correct.
translations.idiomatic: At hall feasts without frame bells and chimes, the flute's fixed tuning makes all string songs follow it.

sentences.zh: 是為笛猶鍾磬，宜必合於律呂。

translations.literal: Thus the flute is like bells and chimes and ought necessarily to accord with pitch pipes and tones.
translations.idiomatic: The flute, like bells and chimes, must accord with pitch pipes and tones.

sentences.zh: 如和所對，直以意造，率短一寸，七孔聲均，不知其皆應何律。

translations.literal: As for He's reply, he simply made them by inclination, generally shortening by one inch; the seven holes sound even, not knowing to which pitch standard each responds.
translations.idiomatic: He's method was mere inclination, usually shortening by an inch; seven even holes with no knowledge of which standard each matched.

sentences.zh: 調與不調，無以檢正。

translations.literal: Whether in tune or not, there is no means to test and correct.
translations.idiomatic: There was no way to test or correct tuning.

sentences.zh: 唯取竹之鳴者，為無法制。

translations.literal: Only taking bamboo that sounds—this is without legal system.
translations.idiomatic: Taking whatever bamboo happens to sound was lawless.

sentences.zh: 輒令部郎劉秀、鄧昊、王豔、魏邵等與笛工參共作笛，[33]工人造其形，律者定其聲，然後器象有制，音均和協。

translations.literal: They then ordered the department officers Liu Xiu, Deng Hao, Wang Yan, Wei Shao, and others to make flutes together with flute craftsmen; [33] craftsmen made the form, pitch specialists fixed the sound—then the instrument had system and the tones were evenly harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: They ordered Liu Xiu, Deng Hao, Wang Yan, Wei Shao, and flute craftsmen to make flutes together; [33] craftsmen shaped them, specialists fixed the tones—so instruments had system and sounds harmonized.

sentences.zh: 又問和：「若不知律呂之義，作樂音均高下清濁之調，當以何名之？

translations.literal: They again asked He: 「If one does not know the meaning of pitch pipes and tones, by what should one name the tuning of high and low, clear and murky in making music?
translations.idiomatic: They asked: 「Without knowing pitch theory, what names should high-low and clear-murky tuning bear?

sentences.zh: 」和辭：「每合樂時，隨歌者聲之清濁，用笛有長短。

translations.literal: 」He replied: 「Each time music was assembled, following whether the singer's voice was clear or murky, one used flutes long or short.
translations.idiomatic: 」He replied: 「When assembling music we followed the singer's voice, using long or short flutes.

sentences.zh: 假令聲濁者用三尺二笛，因名曰此三尺二調也。

translations.literal: Suppose the voice was murky and one used a three-foot-two flute—one therefore named it the three-foot-two tuning.
translations.idiomatic: A murky voice might use a three-foot-two flute, hence the 'three-foot-two tuning.'

sentences.zh: 聲清者用二尺九笛，因名曰此二尺九調也。

translations.literal: A clear voice used a two-foot-nine flute—one therefore named it the two-foot-nine tuning.
translations.idiomatic: A clear voice used a two-foot-nine flute, hence the 'two-foot-nine tuning.'

sentences.zh: 漢、魏相傳，施行皆然。

translations.literal: Han and Wei transmitted and practiced it—all were so.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei transmitted this practice throughout.

sentences.zh: 」案周禮奏六樂，乃奏黃鍾，歌大呂；

translations.literal: 」Examining the Rites of Zhou on performing the six kinds of music: then play the Yellow Bell, sing the Great Lu;
translations.idiomatic: 」The Rites of Zhou on the six musics: play Yellow Bell, sing Great Lu;

sentences.zh: 乃奏太蔟，歌應鍾。

translations.literal: then play the Great Cu, sing the Responding Bell.
translations.idiomatic: play Great Cu, sing Responding Bell.

sentences.zh: 皆以律呂之義，紀歌奏清濁。

translations.literal: All use the meaning of pitch pipes and tones to record the clear and murky of song and performance.
translations.idiomatic: All record song and performance in terms of pitch standards, clear and murky.

sentences.zh: 而和所稱以二尺三尺為名，雖漢、魏用之，俗而不典。

translations.literal: What He called by two feet and three feet as names, although Han and Wei used them, is vulgar and not canonical.
translations.idiomatic: Naming tunings by two or three feet, though Han and Wei used it, is vulgar and uncanonical.

sentences.zh: 部郎劉秀、鄧昊等以律作笛，三尺二寸者，應無射之律，若宜用長笛，執樂者曰「請奏無射」。

translations.literal: The department officers Liu Xiu, Deng Hao, and others, making flutes by pitch standards: three feet two inches responds to the Untempered Pitch standard; if a long flute is needed, the music director says, 'Please perform Untempered Pitch.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiu and Deng Hao made flutes by standard: three feet two inches matches Untempered Pitch—the director would say, 'Perform Untempered Pitch.'

sentences.zh: 周語曰：「無射所以宣布哲人之令德，示民軌儀也。

translations.literal: The Discourses of Zhou says: 「Untempered Pitch is what proclaims the wise man's virtuous command and shows the people their measure.
translations.idiomatic: The Discourses of Zhou: 「Untempered Pitch proclaims the sage's command and shows the people their measure.

sentences.zh: 」二尺八寸四分四釐應黃鍾之律，若宜用短笛，執樂者曰「請奏黃鍾」。

translations.literal: 」Two feet eight inches four fen four li responds to the Yellow Bell standard; if a short flute is needed, the music director says, 'Please perform Yellow Bell.'
translations.idiomatic: 」Two feet eight inches four fen four li matches Yellow Bell—the director would say, 'Perform Yellow Bell.'

sentences.zh: 周語曰：「黃鍾所以宣養六氣九德也。

translations.literal: The Discourses of Zhou says: 「Yellow Bell is what nourishes the six breaths and nine virtues.
translations.idiomatic: The Discourses of Zhou: 「Yellow Bell nourishes the six breaths and nine virtues.

sentences.zh: 」是則歌奏之義，當合經禮，考之古典，於制為雅。

translations.literal: 」Thus the meaning of song and performance should conform to the classic rites; examined against ancient canon, in regulation it is refined.
translations.idiomatic: 」Song and performance should follow the classic rites; by ancient canon this is refined.

sentences.zh: 書曰：「予欲聞六律五聲八音，在治忽。

translations.literal: The Documents says: 「I wish to hear the six pitch standards, five tones, and eight materials of sound, in governance and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents: 「I wish to hear the six standards, five tones, and eight sounds—in order and disorder.

sentences.zh: 」[34]周禮載六律六同。

translations.literal: 」[34] The Rites of Zhou record six pitch standards and six unisons.
translations.idiomatic: 」[34] The Rites of Zhou record six standards and six unisons.

sentences.zh: 禮記又曰：「五聲十二律，還相為宮。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites also says: 「The five tones and twelve pitch standards revolve to serve as one another's gong.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites: 「The five tones and twelve standards revolve as one another's gong.

sentences.zh: 」劉歆、班固纂律曆志，亦紀十二律。

translations.literal: 」Liu Xin and Ban Gu in compiling the Treatises on Pitch Pipes and the Calendar also recorded the twelve pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: 」Liu Xin and Ban Gu recorded the twelve standards in their treatises.

sentences.zh: 唯京房始創六十律，至章帝時，其法已亡；

translations.literal: Only Jing Fang first created the sixty pitch standards; by Emperor Zhang's time his method was already lost;
translations.idiomatic: Only Jing Fang created sixty standards; by Emperor Zhang's time the method was lost;

sentences.zh: 蔡邕雖追紀其言，[35]亦曰「今無能為者」。

translations.literal: although Cai Yong traced and recorded his words, [35] he also said, 'Today there is no one who can do it.'
translations.idiomatic: though Cai Yong recorded his words, [35] he said, 'Today no one can do it.'

sentences.zh: 依案古典及今音家所用六十律者，無施於樂。

translations.literal: Examining ancient canon and what pitch specialists use today, the sixty pitch standards have no application in music.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient canon and modern practice show the sixty standards have no use in music.

sentences.zh: 謹依典記，以五聲十二律還相為宮之法，制十二笛象，記注圖側，如別。

translations.literal: Respectfully following canonical records, by the method of the five tones and twelve pitch standards revolving as gong, we made models of twelve flutes, with diagrams and notes on the side, as separately [appended].
translations.idiomatic: Following canonical records, we made twelve flute models by the five-tone twelve-standard cycle, with diagrams appended separately.

sentences.zh: 省圖，不如視笛之了，故復重作蕤賓伏孔笛。

translations.literal: Viewing the diagram is not as clear as seeing the flute itself; therefore we again made a Flaccid Guest stopped-hole flute.
translations.idiomatic: Diagrams are less clear than the flute itself; we therefore remade a Flaccid Guest stopped-hole flute.

sentences.zh: 其制云：

translations.literal: Its specifications read:
translations.idiomatic: Its specifications read:

sentences.zh: 黃鍾之笛，正聲應黃鍾，下徵應林鍾，長二尺八寸四分四釐有奇。

translations.literal: The Yellow Bell flute: correct sound responds to Yellow Bell, lower zhi responds to Lin Bell, length two feet eight inches four fen four li and a fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell flute: correct sound on Yellow Bell, lower zhi on Lin Bell, length two feet eight inches four fen four li and a fraction.

sentences.zh: 〈周語曰：「黃鍾所以宣養六氣九德也。

translations.literal: 〈The Discourses of Zhou says: 「Yellow Bell is what nourishes the six breaths and nine virtues.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Discourses of Zhou: 「Yellow Bell nourishes the six breaths and nine virtues.

sentences.zh: 」正聲調法，[36]以黃鍾為宮，則姑洗為角。

translations.literal: 」Correct-sound tuning method, [36] taking Yellow Bell as gong, then Gu Xian is jue.
translations.idiomatic: 」Correct-sound method: [36] with Yellow Bell as gong, Gu Xian is jue.

sentences.zh: 翕笛之聲應姑洗，故以四角之長為黃鍾之笛也。

translations.literal: The closed-flute sound responds to Gu Xian; therefore take the length of four corners as the Yellow Bell flute.
translations.idiomatic: The closed sound matches Gu Xian; hence the Yellow Bell flute length equals four corner measures.

sentences.zh: 其宮聲正而不倍，故曰正聲。〉

translations.literal: Its gong sound is correct and not doubled; therefore it is called correct sound.〉
translations.idiomatic: Its gong tone is correct, not doubled; hence 'correct sound.'〉

sentences.zh: 正聲調法，黃鍾為宮，

translations.literal: Correct-sound tuning method, Yellow Bell as gong,
translations.idiomatic: Correct-sound method, Yellow Bell as gong,

sentences.zh: 〈第一孔。〉

translations.literal: 〈First hole.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈First hole.〉

sentences.zh: 應鍾為變宮，

translations.literal: Responding Bell as altered gong,
translations.idiomatic: Responding Bell as altered gong,

sentences.zh: 〈第二孔。〉

translations.literal: 〈Second hole.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Second hole.〉

sentences.zh: 南呂為羽，

translations.literal: Southern Lu as yu,
translations.idiomatic: Southern Lu as yu,

sentences.zh: 〈第三孔。〉

translations.literal: 〈Third hole.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Third hole.〉

sentences.zh: 林鍾為徵，

translations.literal: Lin Bell as zhi,
translations.idiomatic: Lin Bell as zhi,

sentences.zh: 〈第四孔。〉

translations.literal: 〈Fourth hole.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Fourth hole.〉

sentences.zh: 蕤賓為變徵，

translations.literal: Flaccid Guest as altered zhi,
translations.idiomatic: Flaccid Guest as altered zhi,

sentences.zh: 〈第五附孔。〉

translations.literal: 〈Fifth auxiliary hole.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Fifth auxiliary hole.〉

sentences.zh: 姑洗為角，

translations.literal: Gu Xian as jue,
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xian as jue,

sentences.zh: 〈笛體中聲。〉

translations.literal: 〈Sound in the body of the flute.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Tone within the flute body.〉

sentences.zh: 太蔟為商。

translations.literal: Great Cu as shang.
translations.idiomatic: Great Cu as shang.

sentences.zh: 〈笛後出孔也。

translations.literal: 〈Hole at the rear of the flute.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Rear hole of the flute.

sentences.zh: 商聲濁於角，當在角下，而角聲以在體中，故上其商孔，令在宮上，清於宮也。

translations.literal: Shang sound is murkier than jue and should be below jue, but because jue sound is in the body, the shang hole is placed above gong, clearer than gong.
translations.idiomatic: Shang is murkier than jue and should lie below jue, but because jue is in the body the shang hole is placed above gong, clearer than gong.

sentences.zh: 然則宮商正也，餘聲皆倍也。

translations.literal: Thus gong and shang are correct; the rest of the sounds are all doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Gong and shang are correct; other tones are doubled.

sentences.zh: 是故從宮以下，孔轉下轉濁也。

translations.literal: Therefore from gong downward, holes turn lower and murkier.
translations.idiomatic: Below gong, holes descend and grow murkier.

sentences.zh: 此章說笛孔上下次第之名也。

translations.literal: This section explains the names of the flute holes in order above and below.
translations.idiomatic: This section names the flute holes in order from top to bottom.

sentences.zh: [37]下章說律呂相生，笛之制也。〉

translations.literal: [37] The next section explains mutual generation of pitch pipes and flute construction.〉
translations.idiomatic: [37] The next section treats pitch generation and flute construction.〉

sentences.zh: 正聲調法，黃鍾為宮，

translations.literal: Correct-sound tuning method, Yellow Bell as gong,
translations.idiomatic: Correct-sound method, Yellow Bell as gong,

sentences.zh: 〈作黃鍾之笛，將求宮孔，以姑洗及黃鍾律從笛首下度之，盡二律之長而為孔，則得宮聲也。〉

translations.literal: 〈In making a Yellow Bell flute, to find the gong hole measure down from the head with Gu Xian and Yellow Bell standards; exhaust the length of two standards to make the hole—then obtain gong sound.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈To find the gong hole on a Yellow Bell flute, measure two standards down from the head with Gu Xian and Yellow Bell—then gong is obtained.〉

sentences.zh: 宮生徵，黃鍾生林鍾也。

translations.literal: Gong generates zhi; Yellow Bell generates Lin Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Gong generates zhi; Yellow Bell generates Lin Bell.

sentences.zh: 〈以林鍾之律從宮孔下度之，盡律作孔，則得徵聲也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Measure down from the gong hole with the Lin Bell standard; exhaust the standard to make the hole—then obtain zhi sound.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Measure down from the gong hole by Lin Bell standard to obtain zhi.〉

sentences.zh: 徵生商，林鍾生太蔟也。

translations.literal: Zhi generates shang; Lin Bell generates Great Cu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi generates shang; Lin Bell generates Great Cu.

sentences.zh: 〈以太蔟律從徵孔上度之，盡律以為孔，則得商聲也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Measure up from the zhi hole with the Great Cu standard; exhaust the standard to make the hole—then obtain shang sound.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Measure up from the zhi hole by Great Cu standard to obtain shang.〉

sentences.zh: 商生羽，太蔟生南呂也。

translations.literal: Shang generates yu; Great Cu generates Southern Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Shang generates yu; Great Cu generates Southern Lu.

sentences.zh: 〈以南呂律從商孔下度之，[38]盡律為孔，則得羽聲也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Measure down from the shang hole with the Southern Lu standard; [38] exhaust the standard to make the hole—then obtain yu sound.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Measure down from the shang hole by Southern Lu standard [38] to obtain yu.〉

sentences.zh: 羽生角，南呂生姑洗也。

translations.literal: Yu generates jue; Southern Lu generates Gu Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu generates jue; Southern Lu generates Gu Xian.

sentences.zh: 〈以姑洗律從羽孔上行度之，盡律而為孔，則得角聲也。

translations.literal: 〈Measure up from the yu hole with the Gu Xian standard; exhaust the standard to make the hole—then obtain jue sound.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Measure up from the yu hole by Gu Xian standard to obtain jue.

sentences.zh: 然則出於商孔之上，吹笛者左手所不及也。

translations.literal: Thus it would issue above the shang hole, beyond the left hand of the flute player.
translations.idiomatic: That would lie above the shang hole, beyond the player's left hand.

sentences.zh: 從羽孔下行度之，盡律而為孔，亦得角聲，出於變徵附孔之下，[39]則吹者右手所不逮也，故不作角孔。

translations.literal: Measuring down from the yu hole, exhausting the standard to make the hole, one also obtains jue sound, issuing below the altered-zhi auxiliary hole—[39] then beyond the player's right hand; therefore no jue hole is made.
translations.idiomatic: Measuring down from the yu hole also yields jue below the altered-zhi hole [39], beyond the right hand—so no jue hole is cut.

sentences.zh: 推而下之，復倍其均，是以角聲在笛體中，古之制也。

translations.literal: Pushing downward and again doubling the evenness, therefore jue sound is in the body of the flute—such was the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: Doubling downward places jue in the flute body—the ancient system.

sentences.zh: 音家舊法，雖一倍再倍，[40]但令均同。

translations.literal: The old method of pitch specialists, although doubling once or twice, [40] only made the evenness the same.
translations.idiomatic: Old specialists, though doubling once or twice, [40] only equalized the blend.

sentences.zh: 適足為唱和之聲，無害於曲均故也。

translations.literal: It sufficed for singing in harmony and did not harm the melody's evenness.
translations.idiomatic: That sufficed for harmony without harming melodic balance.

sentences.zh: 周語曰，匏竹利制，議宜，謂便於事用從宜者也。〉

translations.literal: The Discourses of Zhou says that gourd and bamboo profit by regulation and convenience—meaning suitable for use according to circumstance.〉
translations.idiomatic: Discourses of Zhou: gourd and bamboo are regulated for convenience—suited to practical use.〉

sentences.zh: 角生變宮，姑洗生應鍾也。

translations.literal: Jue generates altered gong; Gu Xian generates Responding Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Jue generates altered gong; Gu Xian generates Responding Bell.

sentences.zh: 〈上句所謂當為角孔而出商上者，[41]墨點識之，以應律也。

translations.literal: 〈The above passage on what should be the jue hole but issues above shang—[41] mark with ink to respond to the standard.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Where jue should be but appears above shang [41], mark in ink to match the standard.

sentences.zh: 從此點下行度之，盡律為孔，[42]則得變宮之聲也。〉

translations.literal: Measuring down from this point, exhausting the standard to make the hole, [42] then obtain altered-gong sound.〉
translations.idiomatic: Measure down from that mark [42] to obtain altered gong.〉

sentences.zh: 變宮生變徵，應鍾生蕤賓也。

translations.literal: Altered gong generates altered zhi; Responding Bell generates Flaccid Guest.
translations.idiomatic: Altered gong generates altered zhi; Responding Bell generates Flaccid Guest.

sentences.zh: 〈以蕤賓律從變宮下度之，盡律為孔，則得變徵之聲。

translations.literal: 〈Measure down from altered gong with the Flaccid Guest standard; exhaust the standard to make the hole—then obtain altered-zhi sound.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Measure down from altered gong by Flaccid Guest standard to obtain altered zhi.

sentences.zh: 十二笛之制，各以其宮為主。

translations.literal: The system of the twelve flutes: each takes its own gong as master.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the twelve flutes takes its own gong as master.

sentences.zh: [43]相生之法，或倍或半，其便事用，[44]例皆一者也。〉

translations.literal: [43] The method of mutual generation, whether doubled or halved for convenient use, [44] in every case follows one pattern.〉
translations.idiomatic: [43] Generation may double or halve for convenience; [44] the pattern is always one.〉

sentences.zh: 下徵調法，林鍾為宮，

translations.literal: Lower-zhi tuning method, Lin Bell as gong,
translations.idiomatic: Lower-zhi method, Lin Bell as gong,

sentences.zh: 〈第四孔也。

translations.literal: 〈Fourth hole.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Fourth hole.

sentences.zh: 本正聲黃鍾之徵。

translations.literal: Originally the zhi of correct-sound Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Originally correct-sound Yellow Bell's zhi.

sentences.zh: 徵清當在宮上，用笛之宜，倍令濁下，故曰下徵。

translations.literal: Zhi clear should be above gong; for flute convenience, doubling makes it murky below—therefore called lower zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi should lie above gong; for the flute, doubling lowers it—hence 'lower zhi.'

sentences.zh: 下徵更為宮者，記所謂「五聲十二律還相為宮」也。

translations.literal: Lower zhi further serving as gong is what the record calls 'the five tones and twelve pitch standards revolving as gong.'
translations.idiomatic: Lower zhi becoming gong is the 'five tones and twelve standards revolving as gong' of the records.

sentences.zh: [45]然則正聲調清，下徵調濁也。〉

translations.literal: [45] Thus correct-sound tuning is clear; lower-zhi tuning is murky.〉
translations.idiomatic: [45] Correct sound is clear; lower zhi murky.〉

sentences.zh: 南呂為商，

translations.literal: Southern Lu as shang,
translations.idiomatic: Southern Lu serves as shang,

sentences.zh: 〈第三孔也。

translations.literal: 〈Third hole.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The third hole.

sentences.zh: [46]本正聲黃鍾之羽，今為下徵之商。〉

translations.literal: [46] Originally the yu of correct-sound Yellow Bell, now the shang of lower zhi.〉
translations.idiomatic: [46] In correct sound this was Yellow Bell's yu; in lower zhi it is shang.〉

sentences.zh: 應鍾為角，

translations.literal: Responding Bell as jue,
translations.idiomatic: Responding Bell serves as jue,

sentences.zh: 〈第二孔也。

translations.literal: 〈Second hole.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The second hole.

sentences.zh: 本正聲黃鍾之變宮，今為下徵之角也。〉

translations.literal: Originally the altered gong of correct-sound Yellow Bell, now the jue of lower zhi.〉
translations.idiomatic: Originally Yellow Bell's altered gong in correct sound; now lower zhi's jue.〉

sentences.zh: 黃鍾為變徵，

translations.literal: Yellow Bell as altered zhi,
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell serves as altered zhi,

sentences.zh: 〈下徵之調，林鍾為宮，大呂當變徵。

translations.literal: 〈In lower-zhi tuning, Lin Bell is gong; Great Lu should be altered zhi.
translations.idiomatic: 〈In lower-zhi tuning Lin Bell is gong and Great Lu should be altered zhi.

sentences.zh: 而黃鍾笛本無大呂之聲，故假用黃鍾以為變徵也。

translations.literal: But the Yellow Bell flute has no Great Lu sound, so Yellow Bell is borrowed for altered zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Bell flute lacks a Great Lu tone, so Yellow Bell stands in for altered zhi.

sentences.zh: 假用之法：當變徵之聲，則俱發黃鍾及太蔟、應鍾三孔。

translations.literal: The method of borrowing: when seeking altered zhi, blow together the Yellow Bell, Great Cu, and Responding Bell holes.
translations.idiomatic: To borrow it: for altered zhi, sound Yellow Bell, Great Cu, and Responding Bell together.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾濁而太蔟清，[47]大呂律在二律之間，俱發三孔而微磑𥖪之，[48]則得大呂變徵之聲矣。

translations.idiomatic: Kui had built his pitch pipes on that longer measure, which caused the loss of true pitch.

sentences.zh: 至是搜得此鐸，以調律呂焉。

sentences.zh: 正聲調法 「正聲」各本並作「主聲」，據晉志改。

translations.literal: This section explains the names of flute holes in order above and below: 'in order' in the Hundred-Patch edition reads 'great pitch standard'; Beijian, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read 'large pitch standard'; now changed according to the Jin Treatise.
